title: Palindrome Number
description: Given an integer x, check whether it reads the same forward and backward.
example: Input: 121 Output: true Input: -121 Output: false
brute: Convert the number to a string, reverse it, and compare both strings.
optimized: Reverse only half of the number and compare the two halves. Negative numbers are not palindromes.

title: Plus One
description: An integer is stored as an array of digits. Add 1 and return the resulting digits.
brute: Convert the digits to a numeric/string-based big integer, add one, then convert back.
optimized: Start from the last digit. Increment if it is below 9; otherwise make it 0 and carry left. If all digits are 9, create a new array beginning with 1.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Factorial Trailing Zeroes
description: Given n, return the number of trailing zeroes in n!.
brute: Compute the factorial and repeatedly divide by 10 while the last digit is zero.
optimized: Every trailing zero needs a factor 10 = 2 × 5. Factorials contain more 2s than 5s, so count factors of 5: n/5 + n/25 + n/125 + ....
bruteCost: Time At least O(n) and factorial becomes extremely large | Space Depends on factorial representation

title: Sqrt(x)
description: Return the integer part of the square root of a non-negative integer x.
brute: Try integers from 1 upward until the square becomes greater than x.
optimized: Binary-search the answer between 1 and x. Keep the largest value whose square is <= x.

title: Pow(x, n)
description: Calculate x^n, where n can also be negative.
example: Input: x = 2, n = 10 Output: 1024 Input: x = 2, n = -2 Output: 0.25
brute: Multiply x by itself |n| times, then take the reciprocal for a negative exponent.
optimized: Use binary exponentiation. Square the base and halve the exponent each step; multiply the result when the current exponent bi t is odd.

title: Fraction to Recurring Decimal
description: Convert numerator / denominator to a decimal string. Put repeating decimal digits inside parentheses.
brute: Perform long division and keep previous remainders in a list; scan the list to detect a repeated remainder.
optimized: Store remainder -> result position in a hash map. When a remainder repeats, the decimal digits from its previous position form the repeating part.

title: GCD / LCM
description: Find the greatest common divisor and least common multiple of two positive integers.
brute: Start at min(a,b) and move downward until a value divides both numbers.
optimized: Use Euclid's algorithm: repeatedly replace (a,b) with (b,a % b). Then LCM = (a / GCD) × b.

title: GCD of Strings
description: Return the largest string that can be repeated to form both input strings.
brute: Try common prefixes from longest to shortest and check whether repeating each prefix forms both strings.
optimized: If str1 + str2 != str2 + str1, no common base exists. Otherwise return the prefix whose length is gcd(len1,len2).
optimizedCost: Time O(n+m) | Space O(n+m) due to concatenation

title: Count Primes
description: Count the prime numbers strictly smaller than n.
brute: For every number from 2 to n-1, test divisibility up to its square root.
optimized: Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes. Mark multiples of every prime as composite.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log log n) | Space O(n)

title: Ugly Number
description: Check whether a positive integer has no prime factors other than 2, 3, and 5.
example: Input: 6 Output: true Input: 14 Output: false
brute: Factorize the number and verify that every prime factor belongs to {2,3,5}.
optimized: Repeatedly divide by 2, then 3, then 5 while divisible. The number is ugly if the final value is 1.

title: Integer to Roman
description: Convert an integer into its Roman numeral representation.
brute: Repeatedly subtract individual Roman values while manually handling subtractive cases.
optimized: Store Roman value-symbol pairs in descending order, including 900=CM, 400=CD, etc. Greedily consume the largest possible value.
bruteCost: Time O(n) conceptually | Space O(1) excluding output
optimizedCost: Time O(1) for the standard Roman range | Space O(1)

title: Roman to Integer
description: Convert a valid Roman numeral string into an integer.
brute: Explicitly check all special pairs such as IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, and CM.
optimized: If the current symbol value is smaller than the next symbol, subtract it; otherwise add it.

title: Excel Sheet Column Number
description: Convert an Excel column title such as AB into its column number.
brute: Convert each character to its value and multiply it by the required power of 26.
optimized: Treat the title like a base-26 number: result = result * 26 + currentValue.

title: Excel Sheet Column Title
description: Convert a positive column number into its Excel title.
brute: Determine each positional base-26 value separately.
optimized: Since Excel uses 1..26 rather than 0..25, do n--, take n % 26, append the character, and divide by 26.
bruteCost: Time O(log₂₆ n) | Space O(log₂₆ n)
optimizedCost: Time O(log₂₆ n) | Space O(log₂₆ n) for output

title: Pascal's Triangle
description: Generate the first numRows of Pascal's Triangle.
brute: Compute each cell using the combination formula nCr independently.
optimized: Build every row from the previous row: interior values are the sum of the two values above them.
bruteCost: Time More than O(n²) if combinations are recalculated | Space O(n²) for output
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n²) for output

title: Max Points on a Line
description: Given 2D points, return the maximum number of points that lie on one straight line.
brute: Choose every pair of points as a line and check every other point against that line.
optimized: Use each point as an anchor. Compute normalized slopes to all other points and count equal slopes with a hash map.

title: Check if ith Bit is Set
description: Given a number n and bit position i, determine whether the ith bit is 1.
brute: Convert the number to binary text and inspect the required bit position.
optimized: Create a mask 1 << i and check (n & mask) != 0.
bruteCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(log n)

title: Power of Two
description: Check whether a positive integer is an exact power of 2.
example: Input: 16 Output: true Input: 18 Output: false
brute: Repeatedly divide by 2; if the value reaches 1 without a remainder, it is a power of two.
optimized: A power of two has exactly one set bit, so check n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0.

title: Complement of Base 10 Integer
description: Flip every bit in the binary representation of a non-negative integer and return the resulting value.
brute: Convert to binary text, flip 0/1, then convert back.
optimized: Build a mask containing 1s only across the significant bits and compute (~n) & mask.
bruteCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(log n)
optimizedCost: Time O(log n) to build mask | Space O(1)

title: Extract / Set / Clear / Remove Bit
description: Perform common operations on a particular bit position of an integer.
brute: Convert to binary characters, modify the required position, then convert back.
optimized: Use masks: check with &, set with |, clear with & ~mask, toggle with ^.
bruteCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(log n)

title: Copy Set Bits in a Range
description: Copy all set bits from one number to another only within a given bit range.
example: Input: x = 10, y = 13, range = [1,3] Output: x after copying selected set bits from y
brute: Inspect every bit in the range and individually set the corresponding bit in x if it is set in y.
optimized: Build one mask covering the range, extract y & mask, and OR it into x.

title: Swap Odd and Even Bits
description: Swap bits at every adjacent odd/even bit position.
example: Input: 23 (10111) Output: value after swapping adjacent bit positions
brute: Read each adjacent bit pair and reconstruct the result.
optimized: Mask odd and even positions separately, shift one mask left and the other right, then combine them.
bruteCost: Time O(number of bits) | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(1) for fixed-width integers | Space O(1)

title: Number of 1 Bits
description: Count the set bits (1s) in an integer.
brute: Inspect every bit using right shift and & 1.
optimized: Repeatedly remove the lowest set bit using n = n & (n - 1) and count iterations.
bruteCost: Time O(number of bits) | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(number of set bits) | Space O(1)

title: Counting Bits
description: For every number from 0 to n, return its number of set bits.
brute: Count bits separately for every number.
optimized: Reuse previous answers: bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1) or bits[i] = bits[i & (i-1)] + 1.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n) output

title: Longest Consecutive 1s
description: Find the longest run of consecutive 1 bits in the binary representation of a number.
brute: Convert to binary string and scan for the longest run of 1s.
optimized: Repeatedly apply n = n & (n << 1); each iteration reduces every run of consecutive 1s by one.
bruteCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(log n)

title: Single Number
description: Every element appears twice except one. Return the unique element.
brute: Use a frequency map and return the value with count 1.
optimized: XOR all numbers. Pairs cancel because x ^ x = 0.

title: Single Number II
description: Every element appears three times except one element that appears once. Return it.
brute: Count values with a hash map.
optimized: Count each of the 32 bit positions modulo 3, or use the ones/twos bit-state technique.

title: Single Number III
description: Every element appears twice except two unique numbers. Return those two numbers.
brute: Count frequencies and return the two values appearing once. Brute Force: Count frequencies and return the two values appearing once.
optimized: XOR everything to get a ^ b. Use one differing set bit to split numbers into two groups, then XOR each group.

title: Missing Number
description: An array contains n distinct numbers from 0..n with one value missing. Return the missing value.
brute: Put all numbers in a set and scan 0..n for the absent value.
optimized: XOR all indexes 0..n and all array values. Equal values cancel, leaving the missing number.

title: Maximum Subset XOR
description: Choose a subset whose XOR value is as large as possible.
brute: Generate every subset and calculate its XOR.
optimized: Build a XOR linear basis using Gaussian-elimination-style bit operations, then greedily maximize the result.
bruteCost: Time O(2^n × n) | Space O(n) recursion
optimizedCost: Time O(n × B) where B is bit width | Space O(B)

title: XOR of 1 to N / XOR Range
description: Compute XOR over 1..n, or over a range [L,R].
brute: XOR every number in the requested range.
optimized: XOR from 1..n follows a repeating pattern based on n % 4. Range XOR is xor(1..R) ^ xor(1..L-1).

title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
description: Return the bitwise AND of every integer in [left,right].
brute: AND every number in the interval.
optimized: Right-shift both endpoints until they become equal; the remaining common prefix is the answer, shifted back.
optimizedCost: Time O(number of differing bits) | Space O(1)

title: Power Set Using Bits
description: Generate all subsets of an array using a bitmask.
brute: Use recursive take/skip backtracking.
optimized: Iterate masks from 0 to (1<<n)-1; bit i decides whether element i is included.
bruteCost: Time O(n × 2^n) | Space O(n) recursion excluding output
optimizedCost: Time O(n × 2^n) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Sum of Two Integers
description: Add two integers without using + or -.
brute: Simulate addition bit by bit while manually tracking carry.
optimized: a ^ b gives sum without carry; (a & b) << 1 gives carry. Repeat until carry becomes zero.

title: Divide Two Integers
description: Divide two integers without using multiplication, division, or modulo.
brute: Repeatedly subtract the divisor from the dividend.
optimized: Use left shifts to subtract the largest doubled divisor that fits into the remaining dividend.
optimizedCost: Time O(log |dividend|) to O(log² |dividend|) depending on implementation | Space O(1)

title: Square Without *, /, pow()
description: Compute the square of an integer without multiplication, division, or pow.
brute: Add the number to itself |n| times.
optimized: Use bit decomposition: recursively/iteratively express the number as even or odd and build the square using shifts and additi ons.
optimizedCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(log n) recursive or O(1) iterative

title: Swap Two Numbers Without Third Variable
description: Swap two integer values without using an extra variable.
example: Input: a = 5, b = 9 Output: a = 9, b = 5
brute: Normally use a temporary variable.
optimized: Use XOR: a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b.
bruteCost: Time O(1) | Space O(1) extra variable

title: Add Binary
description: Add two binary strings and return their binary sum.
brute: Convert both strings to decimal, add them, and convert back; this can overflow for large input.
optimized: Add from right to left using two pointers and a carry, exactly like decimal addition.

title: Reverse Bits
description: Reverse the bits of a fixed-width integer.
brute: Convert to a fixed-width binary string, reverse it, then convert back.
optimized: Repeatedly extract the lowest bit and append it to the result by shifting the result left.

title: Decimal to Binary
description: Convert a decimal integer to binary representation.
brute: Repeatedly divide by 2, store remainders, then reverse them.
optimized: Read the significant bits directly using shifts and masks.
bruteCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(log n)
optimizedCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(log n) for output

title: Binary to Decimal
description: Convert a binary representation to its decimal value.
brute: Multiply each bit by its explicit power of two and sum.
optimized: Process left to right using result = result * 2 + bit.

title: Convert Number to Hexadecimal
description: Convert an integer to hexadecimal representation.
brute: Repeatedly divide by 16 and convert remainders to hexadecimal digits.
optimized: Process four bits at a time with n & 15 and unsigned right shift by 4.
bruteCost: Time O(log₁₆ n) | Space O(log₁₆ n)

title: Max Consecutive Ones
description: Given a binary array, return the maximum number of consecutive 1s.
brute: Start at every index and count consecutive 1s forward.
optimized: Scan once, maintain the current run of 1s, reset on 0, and track the maximum.

title: Rotate Array
description: Rotate an array to the right by k positions.
brute: Move the last element to the front one step at a time, k times.
optimized: Normalize k, reverse the whole array, reverse the first k elements, then reverse the remaining elements.

title: Check if Array is Sorted and Rotated
description: Determine whether an array was non-decreasing and then possibly rotated.
brute: Try every rotation and test whether the rotated array is sorted.
optimized: Count positions where nums[i] > nums[(i+1)%n]. A sorted-rotated array can have at most one such break.

title: Kids With Greatest Number of Candies
description: For each child, determine whether giving all extra candies to that child makes their total at least the current maximum.
brute: For every child, scan all other children to find the maximum and compare.
optimized: Find the global maximum once, then check candies[i] + extra >= max for every child.

title: Element With Left Smaller and Right Greater
description: Find an element such that every value on its left is smaller and every value on its right is greater.
brute: For every index, scan all left values and all right values.
optimized: Precompute prefix maximums and suffix minimums, then find an index satisfying leftMax < nums[i] < rightMin.

title: Rearrange Array Alternately
description: For a sorted array, rearrange values as maximum, minimum, second maximum, second minimum, and so on.
brute: Use an extra array and two pointers at the ends.
optimized: Encode two values in each array position using a multiplier larger than the maximum value, then decode later.

title: Wiggle Sort II
description: Rearrange numbers so nums[0] < nums[1] > nums[2] < nums[3]....
brute: Sort the array and fill low/high values into alternating positions using extra space.
optimized: Find the median with QuickSelect and use virtual indexing with three-way partitioning.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Convert Array Into Zigzag Fashion
description: Rearrange values so a < b > c < d > e....
example: Input: [4,3,7,8,6,2,1] Output: one valid zigzag arrangement
brute: Sort and then swap adjacent pairs.
optimized: Scan once and locally swap adjacent elements whenever the expected < or > relation is violated.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space depends on sort

title: Move Zeroes
description: Move all zeroes to the end while keeping the relative order of non-zero elements.
brute: Copy all non-zero values to a new array, then fill the rest with zeroes.
optimized: Use a write pointer for the next non-zero position, then fill remaining positions with zeroes or swap in place.

title: Remove Element
description: Remove all occurrences of a target value in place and return the new valid length.
brute: Build a new array containing only values not equal to the target.
optimized: Maintain a write index. Whenever the current value is not the target, write it at the next valid position.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
description: Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place so every distinct value appears once.
brute: Put unique elements into a set/list and copy them back.
optimized: Use a slow pointer for the last unique value and a fast pointer to scan the sorted array.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
description: Modify a sorted array so every value appears at most twice.
brute: Count occurrences and build a separate result allowing at most two copies.
optimized: Maintain a write index k; write nums[i] only when k < 2 or nums[i] != nums[k-2].

title: Merge Sorted Array
description: Merge two sorted arrays into the first array, which has enough empty space at its end.
brute: Copy nums2 into the empty positions and sort the whole array.
optimized: Use pointers at the ends of both valid arrays and fill nums1 from the back with the larger value.
bruteCost: Time O((m+n) log(m+n)) | Space depends on sort

title: Contains Duplicate
description: Return whether any value appears at least twice.
brute: Compare every pair.
optimized: Insert values into a hash set; if insertion finds an existing value, return true.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integer values in an unsorted array.
brute: Sort the array and scan consecutive values.
optimized: Put values in a set. Start counting only from numbers whose predecessor x-1 does not exist.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space depends on sort

title: Two Sum
description: Return two indexes whose values add up to the target.
brute: Try every pair.
optimized: While scanning, check whether target - nums[i] is already in a hash map of value -> index.

title: Majority Element
description: Return the element that appears more than n/2 times.
brute: Count every value with a frequency map.
optimized: Use Boyer-Moore voting: maintain one candidate and a counter that increments for matches and decrements otherwise.

title: Range Sum Query Immutable
description: After preprocessing an array, answer many queries asking for the sum between indexes left and right.
brute: Sum all elements in the requested range for every query.
optimized: Build a prefix sum once. Query with prefix[right+1] - prefix[left].
bruteCost: Time O(n) per query | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) preprocessing, O(1) per query | Space O(n)

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description: Count contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k.
brute: Start at every index and extend the subarray while accumulating its sum.
optimized: Maintain a running prefix sum and a map of prefix frequencies. Previous prefix sum-k means the elements between it and the current position sum to k.

title: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals K
description: Find the maximum length of a contiguous subarray whose sum equals k.
brute: Check the sum of every possible subarray.
optimized: Store the earliest index for each prefix sum. If sum-k was seen, the distance gives a valid subarray length.

title: Contiguous Array
description: Find the longest contiguous subarray containing equal numbers of 0s and 1s.
brute: Check every subarray and count zeroes and ones.
optimized: Treat 0 as -1 and 1 as +1. Equal counts produce the same prefix sum; store the first index where each sum appears.

title: Continuous Subarray Sum
description: Determine whether there is a length-at-least-two subarray whose sum is a multiple of k.
brute: Compute every length-at-least-two subarray sum and test % k == 0.
optimized: Store the earliest index for each prefix remainder sum % k. The same remainder at two positions means their difference is divisible by k.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Return an array where each result is the product of all input values except the value at that index, without division.
brute: For every index, multiply all other elements.
optimized: First write prefix products into the result; then scan from right while multiplying by a running suffix product.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding output
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Find the largest possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
brute: Calculate the sum of every possible subarray.
optimized: At each value, choose whether to extend the previous subarray or start a new one: current = max(nums[i], current + nums[i]).
bruteCost: Time O(n²) with running sums | Space O(1)

title: Maximum Product Subarray
description: Return the maximum product of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
brute: Compute the product of every subarray.
optimized: Track both maximum and minimum products ending at each position because a negative number can swap their roles.

title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
description: Find the maximum subarray sum when the array is circular.
brute: Try every starting index and extend up to n elements circularly.
optimized: Answer is either the normal Kadane maximum or totalSum - minimumSubarraySum. Handle the all-negative case separately.

title: H-Index
description: Return the largest h such that at least h papers have at least h citations each.
brute: Try every possible h from 0..n and count papers with at least h citations.
optimized: Use n+1 buckets; citations above n go into bucket n. Scan buckets from high to low until accumulated papers reach the candidate h.

title: Sort Colors
description: Sort an array containing only 0, 1, and 2 in place.
brute: Use a normal sorting algorithm.
optimized: Use Dutch National Flag with low, mid, and high pointers.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space depends on sort

title: Set Mismatch
description: Numbers should contain 1..n, but one number is duplicated and one is missing. Return [duplicate, missing].
brute: Count every number using a frequency array/map.
optimized: Place each value x at index x-1 using cyclic sort, then find the index whose value is incorrect. Negative marking is another O(1)-extra-space option.

title: First Missing Positive
description: Return the smallest missing positive integer from an unsorted array.
brute: Put all positive values in a set, then test 1,2,3....
optimized: Place each value in the range 1..n at index value-1. The first index where nums[i] != i+1 gives the answer.

title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
description: The array contains values in 1..n. Return all values in that range that are missing.
brute: Put every array value in a set and scan 1..n.
optimized: For each value x, mark nums[abs(x)-1] negative. Positive positions after the pass correspond to missing values.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
description: Values lie in 1..n, and some values appear twice. Return all duplicates.
brute: Count frequencies with a set/map.
optimized: For each value x, inspect index abs(x)-1. If that position is already negative, x is a duplicate; otherwise negate it.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Binary Search
description: Find a target in a sorted array and return its index, or -1 if absent.
brute: Scan the array from left to right.
optimized: Compare the target with the middle element and discard half of the search range each step.

title: Search Insert Position
description: In a sorted array, return the target index if found; otherwise return where it should be inserted.
brute: Scan until finding the first value greater than or equal to the target.
optimized: Binary-search for the first position where nums[i] >= target.

title: Find First and Last Position in Sorted Array
description: Return the first and last index of a target in a sorted array.
brute: Scan the full array and record first and last matching positions.
optimized: Run modified binary search twice: once for the first occurrence and once for the last occurrence.

title: Count Occurrences in Sorted Array
description: Count how many times a target occurs in a sorted array.
brute: Scan and count matches.
optimized: Find lower bound and upper bound; count is upperBound - lowerBound.

title: Floor and Ceil in Sorted Array
description: For a target, find the greatest array value <= target and the smallest value >= target.
brute: Scan all values and track the best floor and ceil.
optimized: Use binary search while updating floor when nums[mid] < target and ceil when nums[mid] > target.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Search a target in a sorted array that has been rotated, with distinct values.
brute: Linear scan.
optimized: At each midpoint, one side is guaranteed sorted. Check whether the target lies in that sorted side and discard the other half .

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
description: Search a target in a rotated sorted array that may contain duplicates.
brute: Linear scan.
optimized: Use rotated binary search. When left == mid == right, shrink both ends because duplicates hide which side is sorted.
optimizedCost: Time O(log n) average, O(n) worst case | Space O(1)

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Return the minimum element in a rotated sorted array with distinct values.
brute: Scan all elements and track the minimum.
optimized: Compare nums[mid] with nums[right]. If nums[mid] > nums[right], the minimum is to the right; otherwise it is at mid or to the left.

title: Single Element in a Sorted Array
description: Every value in a sorted array appears twice except one value. Return that single value.
brute: XOR all values or scan pair by pair.
optimized: Before the unique element, pairs begin at even indexes; afterward this alignment changes. Binary -search this parity pattern.

title: Find Peak Element
description: Return any index whose value is greater than its neighbors.
brute: Scan and check every element against neighbors.
optimized: If nums[mid] < nums[mid+1], a peak exists on the right; otherwise a peak exists at mid or on the left.

title: Peak Index in a Mountain Array
description: A mountain array strictly increases then strictly decreases. Return the peak index.
brute: Scan until the sequence stops increasing.
optimized: Binary-search the slope using arr[mid] < arr[mid+1].

title: Find a Peak Element II
description: In a 2D matrix, return a cell greater than its left/right/up/down neighbors.
example: Input: [[1,4],[3,2]] Output: [0,1] or another valid peak
brute: Check every cell against its neighbors.
optimized: Binary-search columns. In the middle column, find the maximum row; compare that cell with left/right to decide which half contains a peak.
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × log cols) | Space O(1)

title: Koko Eating Bananas
description: Find the minimum integer eating speed that lets Koko finish all banana piles within h hours.
brute: Try every speed from 1 to the largest pile and compute required hours.
optimized: Binary-search speed from 1..maxPile. For each speed, calculate whether total required hours are <= h.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log maxPile) | Space O(1)

title: Minimum Days to Make M Bouquets
description: Flowers bloom on given days. Find the minimum day on which m bouquets of k adjacent flowers can be made.
brute: Test every day from the minimum bloom day to the maximum bloom day.
optimized: Binary-search the day. A feasibility scan counts how many bouquets can be made using flowers bloomed by that day.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log range) | Space O(1)

title: Capacity to Ship Packages Within D Days
description: Find the minimum ship capacity needed to send packages in order within days days.
brute: Try capacities from the heaviest package up to the sum of all weights.
optimized: Binary-search capacity between max(weights) and sum(weights). Simulate how many days a candidate capacity needs.
bruteCost: Time O(sum × n) worst case | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log sum) | Space O(1)

title: Split Array Largest Sum
description: Split an array into k non-empty contiguous parts while minimizing the largest part sum.
brute: Try every possible split arrangement recursively.
optimized: Binary-search the maximum allowed part sum between max(nums) and sum(nums). Greedily count how many parts a candidate requires.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log sum) | Space O(1)

title: Aggressive Cows
description: Place k cows in stalls so the minimum distance between any two cows is as large as possible.
brute: Try possible placements and calculate the minimum distance.
optimized: Sort stalls and binary-search the minimum distance. Greedily place each next cow at the earliest stall at least that distance away.
bruteCost: Time Combinational / very high | Space depends on approach
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n + n log range) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Allocate Books
description: Allocate consecutive books among students while minimizing the maximum pages assigned to any student.
brute: Try every possible partition of books among students.
optimized: Binary-search the maximum pages per student. Greedily count students required for each candidate limit.
bruteCost: Time Exponential / combinational | Space recursion dependent
optimizedCost: Time O(n log sum) | Space O(1)

title: Painter's Partition
description: Assign consecutive boards to painters while minimizing the maximum total length painted by one painter.
brute: Try all valid contiguous partitions.
optimized: Binary-search the maximum workload and greedily count how many painters are required.
bruteCost: Time Exponential / combinational | Space recursion dependent
optimizedCost: Time O(n log sum) | Space O(1)

title: Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
description: Choose the smallest positive divisor such that the sum of ceil(nums[i]/divisor) is at most the threshold.
brute: Try every divisor from 1 to the maximum array value. Brute Force: Try every divisor from 1 to the maximum array value.
optimized: Binary-search divisor in 1..maxVal; the computed sum decreases as the divisor increases.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log maxVal) | Space O(1)

title: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
description: Add k gas stations so the maximum distance between adjacent stations becomes as small as possible.
brute: Repeatedly split the currently largest gap using a priority queue.
optimized: Binary-search the maximum allowed distance as a floating-point value. Count how many new stations are needed to make every gap no larger than that value.
bruteCost: Time roughly O((n+k) log n) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n × log(precision range)) | Space O(1)

title: Search a 2D Matrix
description: Rows are sorted, and each row begins after the previous row ends. Determine whether a target exists.
brute: Scan every cell.
optimized: Treat the matrix as one virtual sorted array and binary-search using row = mid / cols, col = mid % cols.

title: Search a 2D Matrix II
description: Every row and every column is individually sorted. Determine whether a target exists.
brute: Search every row or every cell.
optimized: Start at top-right. Move left if the current value is too large, down if it is too small.

title: Matrix Median
description: Find the median of a row-wise sorted matrix.
brute: Copy all values to one array, sort, and take the middle.
optimized: Binary-search the value range. For each candidate value, use upper bounds in each row to count how many elements are <= candidate.
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × log cols × log valueRange) | Space O(1)

title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
description: Rows and columns are sorted. Return the kth smallest matrix element.
brute: Flatten, sort, and return index k-1.
optimized: Binary-search the value range and count how many matrix elements are <= mid using the sorted rows/columns.
bruteCost: Time O(n² log n²) | Space O(n²)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n × log range) or O(n log range) with staircase counting | Space O(1)

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Return the median of two sorted arrays without fully merging them.
brute: Merge the two arrays and take the middle value(s).
optimized: Binary-search a partition in the smaller array so left-side values of both arrays are all <= right-side values.

title: Kth Element of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Return the kth smallest element from two sorted arrays without merging them fully.
brute: Merge until reaching the kth element.
optimized: Binary-search how many elements to take from the smaller array so the left partition contains exactly k values and is valid.
bruteCost: Time O(m+n) worst case | Space O(m+n) or O(1) with two pointers

title: Nth Root of an Integer
description: Find an integer x such that x^n = m, if one exists.
brute: Try candidate roots from 1 upward.
optimized: Binary-search the candidate root and compare mid^n with m, stopping multiplication early if it exceeds m.
bruteCost: Time up to O(m) | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log m) | Space O(1)

title: Kth Missing Positive Number
description: Given an increasing positive array, return the kth missing positive integer.
brute: Walk through positive integers, decrementing k whenever a number is missing.
optimized: At index i, missing count is arr[i] - (i+1). Binary-search the first index where missing count is at least k.

title: H-Index II
description: Citations are sorted ascending. Return the researcher's H-index.
brute: Test every possible h or scan from the end. Brute Force: Test every possible h or scan from the end.
optimized: At index mid, there are n-mid papers from that point onward. Binary-search the first position with citations[mid] >= n-mid.

title: Heaters
description: Houses and heaters lie on a line. Find the minimum heater radius needed to cover every house.
brute: For every house, scan all heaters and find the nearest one.
optimized: Sort heaters. For every house, binary-search its nearest heater(s), compute the minimum distance, and take the maximum over houses.
optimizedCost: Time O(H log H + N log H) | Space depends on sort

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
description: Given a sorted array, return the 1-based indexes of two values whose sum equals the target.
brute: Try every pair.
optimized: Start one pointer at each end. If the sum is too small, move left forward; if too large, move right backward.

title: Valid Palindrome
description: Check whether a string is a palindrome after ignoring non-alphanumeric characters and case.
example: Input: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" Output: true
brute: Build a cleaned lowercase string, reverse it, and compare.
optimized: Use left/right pointers, skip non-alphanumeric characters, and compare lowercase characters directly.

title: Container With Most Water
description: Choose two vertical lines that hold the maximum amount of water.
brute: Calculate area for every pair of lines.
optimized: Start at both ends. Compute area, then move the pointer at the shorter line inward because only increasing the shorter height can improve the result.

title: 3Sum
description: Return all unique triplets whose sum is zero.
brute: Try every triplet and use a set to remove duplicate triplets.
optimized: Sort the array. Fix one number, then use opposite pointers to find pairs summing to its negative while skipping duplicates.
bruteCost: Time O(n³) | Space O(number of answers)
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding output/sort

title: 3Sum Closest
description: Find three numbers whose sum is closest to the target.
brute: Test every triplet and track the sum with the smallest difference from target.
optimized: Sort, fix one element, and use left/right pointers to move the sum toward target.
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: 4Sum
description: Return all unique quadruplets whose sum equals the target.
brute: Try every four-index combination.
optimized: Sort, fix two positions, then use two pointers for the remaining two values while skipping duplicates.
bruteCost: Time O(n⁴) | Space O(number of answers)
optimizedCost: Time O(n³) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Valid Triangle Number
description: Count triplets that can form valid triangle side lengths.
brute: Try every triplet and check the triangle inequality.
optimized: Sort. Fix the largest side and use two pointers; if nums[left] + nums[right] > largest, then all values between left and right-1 also work with right.
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Boats to Save People
description: Each boat carries at most two people and has a weight limit. Return the minimum boats needed.
brute: Try pairing people in many possible combinations.
optimized: Sort. Always place the heaviest remaining person; pair them with the lightest person if they fit together.
bruteCost: Time Exponential in the naive pairing search | Space recursion dependent
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given bar heights, return how much rain water can be trapped between them.
brute: For every position, find the maximum bar to its left and right; trapped water is min(leftMax,rightMax)-height.
optimized: Use two pointers with running leftMax and rightMax. The side with the smaller current boundary determines how much water can safely be calculated. Optimized: Use two pointers with running leftMax and rightMax. The side with the smaller current boundary determines how much water can safely be calculated.

title: Is Subsequence
description: Check whether string s can be formed by deleting characters from t without changing order.
brute: Generate subsequences of t or search repeatedly from the beginning.
optimized: Use one pointer for s and one for t; advance the s pointer whenever characters match.
bruteCost: Time Exponential if generating all subsequences | Space large

title: Find the Duplicate Number
description: An array contains n+1 values in 1..n with exactly one repeated value. Return the duplicate without modifying the array.
brute: Use a set to detect the first repeated value.
optimized: Treat index -> nums[index] as a linked list containing a cycle. Use Floyd's slow/fast pointers to find the cycle entrance, which is the duplicate.

title: Happy Number
description: Repeatedly replace a number with the sum of squares of its digits. Return whether the process reaches 1.
brute: Store every produced value in a set and stop when 1 or a repeated value appears.
optimized: Treat the transformation as a linked-list next function and use slow/fast pointers to detect a cycle.
bruteCost: Time Depends on sequence length | Space O(sequence length)

title: Circular Array Loop
description: Determine whether a circular array contains a cycle of length greater than one where movement stays entirely in one direction .
brute: Start from every index and track visited indexes separately.
optimized: For each unprocessed start, use slow/fast pointers while enforcing one direction; mark processed paths to avoid revisiting th em.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) amortized | Space O(1) if marking in the array

title: 4Sum II
description: Given four arrays, count tuples (i,j,k,l) whose four values sum to zero.
brute: Try every combination across four arrays.
optimized: Store frequencies of all A+B sums, then for every C+D sum add the frequency of its negative.

title: K-Diff Pairs in an Array
description: Count unique pairs whose absolute difference equals k.
brute: Test every pair and store valid value pairs in a set.
optimized: Use a frequency map/set. For k > 0, check whether x+k exists; for k = 0, require frequency greater than one.

title: Next Permutation
description: Rearrange the array into the next lexicographically greater permutation; if none exists, return the smallest permutation.
brute: Generate all permutations, sort them, and locate the next one.
optimized: From the right, find the first decreasing break, swap it with the next larger value on the right, then reverse the suffix.
bruteCost: Time O(n! × n) or worse | Space very large

title: Maximum Average Subarray I
description: Find the maximum average of any contiguous subarray of length k.
brute: Compute the sum of each length-k window from scratch.
optimized: Compute the first window sum once, then slide by adding the incoming value and removing the outgoing value.

title: Substrings of Size Three With Distinct Characters
description: Count length-3 substrings containing three different characters.
brute: Build every size-3 substring and use a set to test uniqueness.
optimized: For each consecutive triple, directly compare the three characters pairwise.
bruteCost: Time O(n) with small constant | Space O(1) because window size is fixed at 3

title: Repeated DNA Sequences
description: Return all length-10 DNA sequences that occur more than once.
brute: Compare every length-10 substring against all later substrings. Brute Force: Compare every length-10 substring against all later substrings.
optimized: Slide a fixed-size window and store seen sequences in a set; add a sequence to the answer when encountered again.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(number of answers)

title: Find the K-Beauty of a Number
description: Count length-k substrings of a number's digits that form a non-zero divisor of the original number.
brute: Extract every size-k digit substring and parse it independently.
optimized: Since digit strings are short, a simple fixed window is already near-optimal; maintain or parse each window once.
optimizedCost: Time O(d) to O(dk) depending on parsing method | Space O(1)

title: Grumpy Bookstore Owner
description: A bookstore owner can suppress grumpiness for exactly minutes consecutive customers. Maximize satisfied customers.
brute: Try the technique starting at every possible window and recompute satisfied customers.
optimized: Count always-satisfied customers once, then find the fixed window with the maximum additional recoverable customers.

title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain From Cards
description: Pick exactly k cards from either end of an array to maximize the score.
brute: Recursively choose left or right k times.
optimized: Total selected score equals total array sum minus one contiguous unselected window of size n-k. Find the minimum such window.

title: Find All Anagrams in a String
description: Return all starting indexes where a substring of s is an anagram of p.
brute: Sort every substring of length |p| and compare with sorted p.
optimized: Keep a frequency count for a fixed-size window and update counts as one character enters and one leaves.
bruteCost: Time O(n × k log k) | Space O(k)

title: Permutation in String
description: Check whether s2 contains any permutation of s1 as a substring.
brute: Sort every length-|s1| substring and compare with sorted s1.
optimized: Slide a fixed-size frequency window and compare character counts/matched counts.
bruteCost: Time O(n × k log k) | Space O(k)

title: Count Occurrences of Anagrams
description: Count how many substrings of the text are anagrams of the pattern.
brute: Sort and compare every pattern-sized substring.
optimized: Maintain pattern frequencies and a fixed-size window, updating counts in O(1) per slide.
bruteCost: Time O(n × k log k) | Space O(k)

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Find the length of the longest substring containing no repeated characters.
brute: Start at every index and extend until a duplicate appears.
optimized: Expand the right pointer while tracking last-seen positions or a set. When a duplicate appears, move the left pointer past the previous occurrence.

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
description: With positive integers, find the minimum length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is at least target.
brute: Start at every index and extend until reaching target.
optimized: Expand right to increase sum; while sum is large enough, update the answer and shrink left.

title: Fruit Into Baskets
description: Find the longest contiguous subarray containing at most two distinct fruit types.
brute: Start from every index and extend while distinct types stay at most two.
optimized: Use a variable window with a frequency map; shrink while the number of distinct values exceeds two.

title: Maximum Consecutive Ones III
description: Return the longest subarray of 1s after flipping at most k zeroes.
brute: Start at each index and extend while counting zeroes until they exceed k.
optimized: Expand right and count zeroes. When zeroes exceed k, shrink from the left until valid again.

title: Subarray Product Less Than K
description: Count contiguous subarrays whose product is less than k, assuming positive values.
brute: Calculate products for every subarray.
optimized: Maintain a product window. Shrink left while product is >= k; every valid right endpoint contributes right-left+1 subarrays.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Find the smallest substring of s containing all characters of t with required frequencies.
brute: Check every substring and test whether it contains all required characters.
optimized: Expand right while updating counts; once all requirements are satisfied, shrink left as much as possible while preserving val idity.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description: Replace at most k characters so a substring consists of one repeated character. Return the maximum length.
brute: Examine every substring, find its most frequent character, and check replacements needed.
optimized: Keep window size and maximum character frequency. A window is valid when windowLength - maxFrequency <= k; shrink otherwise.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) or worse | Space O(alphabet)

title: Subarrays With K Different Integers
description: Count contiguous subarrays containing exactly k distinct integers.
brute: Start from every index, expand, and count distinct values until more than k appear.
optimized: Use exactlyK = atMost(K) - atMost(K-1), where each atMost count is computed with a sliding window.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: Return the maximum value in every window of size k.
brute: Scan every window and compute its maximum.
optimized: Maintain a decreasing deque of candidate indexes. Remove smaller values from the back and expired indexes from the front.

title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Difference <= Limit
description: Find the longest subarray where max - min <= limit.
brute: Check every subarray and compute its min/max.
optimized: Use one decreasing deque for maximums and one increasing deque for minimums. Shrink while their difference exceeds the limit.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) or O(n³) depending on implementation | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(n) worst case

title: Sliding Window Median
description: Return the median of every window of size k.
brute: Sort every window independently.
optimized: Maintain two heaps for lower/upper halves and lazily remove values leaving the window.
bruteCost: Time O(n × k log k) | Space O(k)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log k) | Space O(k)

title: Substring With Concatenation of All Words
description: Find starting indexes where a substring is formed by concatenating all given equal-length words exactly once in any order.
brute: At every index, split the candidate substring into word-sized pieces and compare frequencies.
optimized: Run word-sized sliding windows for each possible offset, maintaining counts of words inside the current window.
bruteCost: Time roughly O(n × numberWords) plus hashing | Space O(numberWords)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) average with hashing | Space O(numberWords)

title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
description: You may increment elements at most k total times. Return the maximum possible frequency of one value.
brute: For every target value, calculate the cost of raising smaller values to it.
optimized: Sort and use a window. Maintain its sum; make every value equal to nums[right]. Shrink while required increments exceed k.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) after sorting | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) due to sorting | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Merge Intervals
description: Merge all overlapping intervals.
brute: Repeatedly compare every interval pair and merge overlaps until no changes remain.
optimized: Sort by start. Compare each interval only with the last merged interval; merge when current.start <= last.end.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) or worse | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n) output

title: Insert Interval
description: Insert a new interval into sorted non-overlapping intervals and merge where necessary.
brute: Add the new interval, sort all intervals, then run merge intervals.
optimized: Add intervals completely before the new interval, merge all overlapping intervals into the new interval, then append the remaining intervals.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Interval List Intersections
description: Given two sorted lists of disjoint intervals, return all intersections between the lists.
brute: Compare every interval in A with every interval in B.
optimized: Use one pointer per list. Intersection is [max(starts), min(ends)] when valid. Advance the interval that ends first.
bruteCost: Time O(mn) | Space O(1) excluding output
optimizedCost: Time O(m+n) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
description: Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest do not overlap.
brute: Explore subsets of intervals and find the largest non-overlapping subset.
optimized: Sort by end time and greedily keep the interval that finishes earliest; Optimized: Sort by end time and greedily keep the interval that finishes earliest; remove intervals that overlap it.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
description: Each balloon is an interval on the x-axis. Find the minimum arrows needed so every interval is hit.
brute: Try many candidate arrow positions and combinations.
optimized: Sort intervals by end. Shoot at the earliest ending position; all intervals containing that point are handled by the same arrow.
bruteCost: Time Exponential / very high | Space depends on search
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Meeting Rooms
description: Determine whether one person can attend all meetings without overlap.
brute: Compare every pair for overlap.
optimized: Sort by start time and check whether any meeting starts before the Optimized: Sort by start time and check whether any meeting starts before the previous meeting ends.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Meeting Rooms II
description: Return the minimum number of meeting rooms required so all meetings can occur.
example: Input: [[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]] Output: 2 Think of it like parking Meetings are cars. A meeting starts → a car enters the parking lot. • A meeting ends → a car leaves. • If another car arrives while all existing spaces are occupied → need another space.•
brute: For every meeting, count how many meetings overlap its time range.
optimized: Sort by start and keep a min-heap of meeting end times. Reuse a room when the earliest-ending meeting has finished.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Minimum Platforms
description: Given train arrival and departure times, return the minimum railway platforms needed so no train waits.
brute: For each train, count how many other trains overlap its stay.
optimized: Sort arrivals and departures separately. Sweep with two pointers; arrival increases active platforms, departure decreases them.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Employee Free Time
description: Each employee has sorted working intervals. Return finite intervals when everyone is free.
brute: Flatten all working intervals, compare time gaps manually, and test whether each gap is free for everyone.
optimized: Flatten and sort all work intervals, merge them, then gaps between merged intervals are common free times. A heap-based k-way merge is also possible.
bruteCost: Time O(N²) in a naive approach | Space O(N)
optimizedCost: Time O(N log N) | Space O(N)

title: Summary Ranges
description: Given sorted unique integers, summarize consecutive runs as a->b or a single value.
brute: For each number, scan forward from scratch to find its consecutive run.
optimized: Scan once, remember the start of the current run, and close the range whenever the next value is not consecutive.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding output
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Jump Game
description: Each value is your maximum jump length. Determine whether the last index is reachable from the first.
brute: From each position, recursively try every possible jump.
optimized: Track the farthest reachable index. If the current index is beyond it, fail; otherwise update the farthest reach.

title: Jump Game II
description: Return the minimum number of jumps required to reach the last index.
brute: Recursively try all jump choices and take the minimum.
optimized: Treat the current reachable range like a BFS level. Scan it to find the farthest next range; when the current range ends, take one jump.

title: Gas Station
description: Find a starting gas station from which a car can complete the circular route, or return -1.
brute: Try every station as the start and simulate the full route.
optimized: If total gas is less than total cost, impossible. Otherwise scan once with a running tank; when it becomes negative, no stati on in the current segment can be the answer, so restart after it.

title: Candy
description: Give each child at least one candy, and children with higher ratings than a neighbor must get more candies. Minimize total ca ndies.
brute: Start everyone at one candy and repeatedly adjust violations until stable.
optimized: Left-to-right handles increasing ratings from the left; right-to-left handles increasing ratings from the right. Take the maximum requirement at each index.
bruteCost: Time Up to O(n²) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(n) or O(1) with a slope-based variant

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: Make one buy and one later sell to maximize profit.
brute: Try every buy/sell pair.
optimized: Track the lowest price seen so far and compute profit if selling today.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
description: You may complete as many buy/sell transactions as needed, but can hold only one stock at a time. Maximize profit.
brute: Recursively decide to buy, sell, or skip on every day.
optimized: Add every positive day-to-day increase; this captures all upward price segments.

title: Largest Number
description: Arrange non-negative integers so their concatenation forms the largest possible number.
brute: Generate every ordering and compare concatenated results.
optimized: Sort strings with comparator (b+a) vs (a+b), then concatenate in that order.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n × k) where k is comparison length | Space O(nk) for strings/output

title: Two City Scheduling
description: Send exactly half of the people to each of two cities while minimizing total travel cost.
brute: Try every choice of which n/2 people go to city A.
optimized: Sort people by (costA - costB). Send the first half to A and the second half to B.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(1) excluding sort

title: Partition Labels
description: Split a string into as many parts as possible so each character appears in at most one part.
brute: Try split positions and verify character overlap across parts.
optimized: Record each character's last occurrence. Scan while extending the current partition end to the furthest last occurrence seen; close when index reaches that end.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) or worse | Space O(alphabet)

title: Increasing Triplet Subsequence
description: Determine whether there exist indices i < j < k with nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k].
brute: Try every triplet.
optimized: Track the smallest first value and smallest possible second value. Any later value greater than both proves a triplet exists.

title: Can Place Flowers
description: Determine whether n new flowers can be planted in a flowerbed without adjacent flowers.
brute: Try possible planting combinations recursively.
optimized: Scan left to right. Plant whenever current, previous, and next positions are empty, then continue.

title: Minimum Number of Refueling Stops
description: Reach a target distance with initial fuel and fuel stations on the route. Return the minimum refueling stops.
brute: Recursively choose whether to stop at each station.
optimized: As you travel, add all reachable station fuel amounts to a max-heap. Whenever fuel is insufficient, take the largest previously reachable fuel supply.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: IPO
description: Complete at most k projects to maximize capital. Each project has a required capital and profit.
example: Input: k=2, w=0, profits=[1,2,3], capital=[0,1,1] Output: 4
brute: At every step, try every currently affordable unused project.
optimized: Sort projects by required capital. Push all currently affordable profits into a max-heap and choose the largest profit each round.
bruteCost: Time Exponential / combinational | Space recursion dependent
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n + k log n) | Space O(n)

title: Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers
description: Hire exactly k workers while paying each at least their minimum wage expectation and using one common wage-to-quality ratio.
brute: Try every group of k workers and calculate its required ratio/cost.
optimized: Sort workers by wage/quality ratio. Maintain the k smallest quality sum with a max-heap; current ratio times quality sum gives cost.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(k)

title: Valid Anagram
description: Check whether two strings contain exactly the same characters with the same frequencies.
brute: Sort both strings and compare them.
optimized: Count character frequencies from the first string and subtract frequencies using the second string.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n) depending on sorting/string conversion

title: Ransom Note
description: Determine whether the ransom note can be built using each magazine character at most once.
brute: For every ransom-note character, search for an unused matching magazine character.
optimized: Count magazine characters, then consume those counts while scanning the ransom note.
bruteCost: Time O(nm) | Space O(m) if marking used characters

title: Longest Palindrome
description: Given letters, return the maximum length of a palindrome that can be built from them.
brute: Try character selections and permutations.
optimized: Use all even counts and the largest even part of odd counts; one odd count may contribute a center character.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Group strings that are anagrams of one another.
brute: Compare each string against existing groups using sorted versions or frequency checks.
optimized: Build a canonical key for each word—either its sorted characters or its character-frequency signature—and group by that key.
bruteCost: Time O(n² × k log k) | Space O(nk)
optimizedCost: Time O(n × k) with frequency keys | Space O(nk)

title: Isomorphic Strings
description: Check whether characters in one string can be consistently mapped one-to-one to characters in another string.
brute: For each position, scan previous mappings to ensure consistency.
optimized: Maintain mappings in both directions so two source characters cannot map to the same target character.

title: Word Pattern
description: Check whether pattern characters and words follow a one-to-one mapping.
example: Input: pattern = "abba", s = "dog cat cat dog" Output: true
brute: For every position, search previous pairs for mapping conflicts.
optimized: Maintain two maps: pattern character to word and word to pattern character.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n) for split words

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Return the longest contiguous substring that is a palindrome.
brute: Generate every substring and check whether it is a palindrome.
optimized: Treat every index and every gap between indexes as a palindrome center and expand outward while characters match.
bruteCost: Time O(n³) | Space O(1) excluding substring creation

title: Palindromic Substrings
description: Count all contiguous substrings that are palindromes.
brute: Generate every substring and check whether it is a palindrome.
optimized: Expand around all odd and even centers and count every successful expansion.

title: Count and Say
description: Generate the nth term where each term describes consecutive groups in the previous term.
brute: Repeatedly rescan groups using substring operations and temporary structures.
optimized: For each term, scan the previous term once, count each consecutive run, and append count + character.
bruteCost: Time proportional to total generated output, with extra substring overhead | Space proportional to generated string size
optimizedCost: Time O(total generated characters) | Space O(current term length)

title: Zigzag Conversion
description: Write a string in a zigzag across a given number of rows and read row by row.
brute: Build a full 2D character grid and simulate the zigzag path.
optimized: Keep one string builder per row and move a row pointer down/up as the direction changes.
bruteCost: Time O(n) | Space O(n) plus grid overhead

title: String Compression
description: Compress consecutive repeated characters in place using the character followed by its count when count > 1.
brute: Build a new compressed string/array from run counts.
optimized: Use a read pointer to identify runs and a write pointer to overwrite the same array.

title: Length of Last Word
description: Return the length of the last word in a string containing words and spaces.
brute: Trim and split the string by spaces, then inspect the final token.
optimized: Scan backward, skip trailing spaces, then count characters until the next space.

title: Reverse Words in a String
description: Reverse the order of words while removing extra spaces.
example: Input: " the sky is blue " Output: "blue is sky the"
brute: Split into words, reverse the list, and join it.
optimized: Scan from right to left, identify each word, and append it directly to the result while skipping extra spaces.

title: Longest Common Prefix
description: Return the longest prefix shared by every string.
brute: Compare every possible prefix of the first string with every other string.
optimized: Compare characters column by column until any string differs or ends.
bruteCost: Time O(n × m²) in a naive substring-based version | Space O(m)
optimizedCost: Time O(total characters inspected) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
description: Return the first index where needle occurs inside haystack, or -1.
brute: Start at every possible position and compare the pattern character by character.
optimized: Use KMP. Precompute the pattern's longest-prefix-suffix table so mismatches reuse previous matching information.

title: Compare Version Numbers
description: Compare version strings where each dot-separated revision is an integer and leading zeroes do not matter.
brute: Split both strings, parse every token, pad missing tokens with zero, then compare.
optimized: Parse revision numbers on the fly with two pointers, avoiding arrays of tokens.

title: Validate IP Address
description: Determine whether a string is a valid IPv4 address, valid IPv6 address, or neither.
brute: Split by both possible separators and apply many ad-hoc checks.
optimized: Detect the separator first, then validate the exact number of groups and the strict rules for each group in one structured pa ss.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(n) if split; O(1) with manual parsing

title: Text Justification
description: Arrange words into lines of exactly maxWidth, distributing spaces so lines are fully justified except the last line.
example: Input: words=["This","is","an","example"], maxWidth=16 Output: lines of length 16
brute: Try many possible word groupings and spacing distributions.
optimized: Greedily pack as many words as fit on each line, then distribute the required spaces evenly, putting extra spaces in earlier gaps.
bruteCost: Time unnecessarily high / combinational if exploring layouts | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(total characters) | Space O(maxWidth) per line excluding output

title: Encode and Decode Strings
description: Design reversible encoding for a list of arbitrary strings, including empty strings and strings containing special characters.
example: Input: ["lint","code","love","you"] Encoded: one combined string Decoded: ["lint","code","love","you"]
brute: Join strings using a separator; this fails if the separator itself occurs in data unless escaping is added.
optimized: Prefix each string with its length and a delimiter, such as 4#lint; decoding first reads the length, then exactly that many characters.
bruteCost: Time O(total characters) | Space O(total characters)
optimizedCost: Time O(total characters) | Space O(total characters) output

title: Delete Node in a Linked List
description: Given direct access to a non-tail node, delete it without access to the head.
brute: With head access, find the previous node and bypass the target; however the problem does not provide the head.
optimized: Copy the next node's value into the current node, then bypass the next node.
bruteCost: Time O(n) if head were available | Space O(1)

title: Delete Middle Node of Linked List
description: Delete the middle node, where the middle is index n/2 using zero-based indexing.
brute: Count the list length, then traverse again to the node before the middle.
optimized: Use slow/fast pointers while keeping the previous slow node; when fast reaches the end, slow is the middle.
bruteCost: Time O(n) with two passes | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) one pass | Space O(1)

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List
description: Remove repeated nodes from a sorted linked list while keeping one copy of each value.
brute: Store seen values in a set and rebuild/filter the list.
optimized: Since the list is sorted, compare each node only with its next node and bypass equal values.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II
description: Remove all values that appear more than once in a sorted list, leaving only values that appeared exactly once.
brute: Count frequencies first, then rebuild a list using only frequency-one values.
optimized: Use a dummy node and detect duplicate runs; connect the previous unique node directly to the first node after each duplicate run.

title: Reverse Linked List
description: Reverse a singly linked list.
brute: Store node values in an array/stack and rebuild or rewrite them in reverse order.
optimized: Maintain prev, curr, and next; redirect each curr.next to prev while advancing.

title: Reverse Linked List II
description: Reverse only the nodes between positions left and right.
brute: Copy nodes/values from the target segment into a stack, then write them back in reverse.
optimized: Use a dummy node, reach the node before left, then reverse the target segment in place and reconnect its ends.

title: Reverse Nodes in K Group
description: Reverse linked-list nodes in groups of size k; leave the final incomplete group unchanged.
brute: Store each full group in an array/stack and reconnect in reverse order.
optimized: Locate each full group boundary, reverse the group pointers in place, reconnect, and continue.

title: Reverse Nodes in Even Length Groups
description: Divide a list into groups of increasing size 1,2,3...; reverse only groups whose actual length is even.
example: Input: 1 -> 1 -> 0 -> 6 Output: list after reversing even-sized groups
brute: Copy every group into a temporary list, reverse even groups, and rebuild.
optimized: Determine each group's actual node count, reverse pointers only when that count is even, and reconnect groups directly.

title: Remove Nth Node From End
description: Remove the nth node from the end of a linked list.
brute: Count length, then remove node at position length-n from the front.
optimized: Use a dummy node and two pointers separated by n+1 positions; when fast reaches the end, slow is before the node to remove.
bruteCost: Time O(n) with two passes | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) one pass | Space O(1)

title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
description: Swap every two adjacent linked-list nodes.
brute: Swap node values pair by pair.
optimized: Use a dummy node and change pointers so each pair a -> b becomes b -> a.

title: Middle of Linked List
description: Return the middle node; for even length, return the second middle.
brute: Count length, then traverse length/2 steps.
optimized: Move slow by one and fast by two; when fast ends, slow is in the middle.
bruteCost: Time O(n) two passes | Space O(1)

title: Linked List Cycle
description: Determine whether a linked list contains a cycle.
example: Input: 3 -> 2 -> 0 -> -4, tail points back to node 2 Output: true
brute: Store visited node references in a set.
optimized: Use Floyd's slow/fast pointers. If they ever meet, a cycle exists.

title: Linked List Cycle II
description: Return the node where a linked-list cycle begins, or null if there is no cycle.
example: Input: 3 -> 2 -> 0 -> -4, tail points to node 2 Output: node 2
brute: Return the first node encountered twice using a visited set.
optimized: First let slow/fast meet inside the cycle. Then move one pointer to head; advancing both one step makes them meet at the cycle entrance.

title: Palindrome Linked List
description: Determine whether the sequence of linked-list values is a palindrome.
brute: Copy values into an array and compare from both ends.
optimized: Find the middle, reverse the second half, and compare the two halves.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
brute: Copy all values, sort them, and build a new list.
optimized: Use a dummy head and repeatedly attach the smaller current node from the two lists.
optimizedCost: Time O(m+n) | Space O(1) excluding output links

title: Merge In Between Linked Lists
description: Replace nodes from positions a..b in one list with an entire second list.
brute: Convert both lists to arrays, construct the combined sequence, then rebuild a list.
optimized: Find the node before a, the node after b, and the tail of list2, then reconnect these three points.

title: Reorder List
description: Transform L0 -> L1 -> ... -> Ln into L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 ....
brute: Store all nodes in an array and reconnect them using indexes from both ends.
optimized: Find the middle, reverse the second half, then alternately merge nodes from the first and reversed second halves.

title: Odd Even Linked List
description: Group nodes at odd positions first, followed by nodes at even positions, preserving relative order within each group.
brute: Build separate arrays/lists for odd and even positions, then combine them.
optimized: Maintain odd, even, and the head of the even chain; relink nodes in one pass.

title: Partition List
description: Rearrange nodes so values less than x come before values greater than or equal to x, preserving relative order.
brute: Copy values into two arrays/lists and rebuild.
optimized: Build two linked chains using dummy heads—one for < x, one for >= x—then connect them.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(1) extra nodes

title: Rotate List
description: Rotate a linked list to the right by k places.
brute: Move the tail node to the front k times.
optimized: Find length, connect tail to head to form a circle, normalize k, then break the circle at the new tail.

title: Swapping Nodes in a Linked List
description: Swap the values/nodes at the kth position from the start and kth from the end.
brute: Store all nodes in an array and access both positions directly.
optimized: Find the kth node from start, then use another pointer so when one reaches the end, the other is the kth from end; swap values.

title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
description: Return the shared node where two singly linked lists intersect by reference.
example: List A: 4 -> 1 -> 8 -> 4 -> 5 List B: 5 -> 6 -> 1 -> 8 -> 4 -> 5 Output: node with value 8
brute: Put all nodes from one list in a set and scan the other list for the first shared reference.
optimized: Use two pointers; when a pointer reaches the end, redirect it to the other list's head. They align after traversing equal tot al distance.

title: Copy List With Random Pointer
description: Deep-copy a linked list whose nodes contain both next and arbitrary random pointers.
example: Input: linked list with random references Output: structurally identical independent copy
brute: Create copy nodes and store original -> copy in a hash map, then connect next/random pointers in a second pass.
optimized: Insert each copied node directly after its original node, set random pointers through original.random.next, then separate the two lists.

title: Add Two Numbers
description: Two linked lists store digits in reverse order. Return a list representing their sum.
brute: Convert both lists to whole numbers, add them, and build a result list; this can overflow for long lists.
optimized: Add corresponding digits node by node with a carry, creating result nodes as you go.
bruteCost: Time O(m+n) | Space proportional to number size

title: Sort List
description: Sort a linked list in ascending order.
brute: Copy values to an array, sort, and write them back.
optimized: Use merge sort: find the middle, recursively sort both halves, then merge them. Linked lists merge without shifting elements.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(log n) recursion

title: Convert Binary Number in Linked List to Integer
description: A linked list stores bits from most significant to least significant. Return its decimal value.
brute: Store bits, then calculate powers of two from right to left.
optimized: Process left to right with result = result * 2 + bit.

title: Convert Sorted List to BST
description: Convert an ascending singly linked list into a height-balanced binary search tree.
example: Input: -10 -> -3 -> 0 -> 5 -> 9 Output: one valid balanced BST
brute: Copy list values into an array and recursively choose middle values.
optimized: Simulate inorder construction using list length and a moving list pointer, building left subtree, root, then right subtree.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(log n) recursion for balanced tree

title: Maximum Twin Sum of a Linked List
description: In an even-length list, pair first with last, second with second-last, etc.; return the maximum pair sum.
brute: Copy values into an array and compare symmetric indexes.
optimized: Find the middle, reverse the second half, and scan both halves together computing pair sums.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Check whether brackets ()[]{} are correctly opened and closed in matching order.
brute: Repeatedly remove occurrences of (), [], and {} until no more changes occur.
optimized: Push opening brackets onto a stack; each closing bracket must match the stack top.

title: Redundant Braces
description: Determine whether an arithmetic expression contains unnecessary parentheses.
brute: Parse and simplify every parenthesized section repeatedly.
optimized: Use a stack. On ), inspect items back to (; if no operator appears, that pair of braces is redundant.

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
description: Evaluate an expression written in postfix notation.
brute: Repeatedly search for an operator, evaluate its two previous operands, and replace the three tokens.
optimized: Push numbers. On an operator, pop the right operand then left operand, apply the operation, and push the result.

title: Basic Calculator
description: Evaluate a valid arithmetic expression containing integers, +, -, parentheses, and spaces.
brute: Recursively locate innermost parentheses, evaluate substrings, and replace them.
optimized: Scan once with a running result, current number, and sign. Push the previous result/sign when entering parentheses and combine when leaving them.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) due to repeated substring work | Space O(n)

title: Simplify Path
description: Convert an absolute Unix path into its canonical form, handling ., .., and repeated slashes.
brute: Repeatedly replace duplicated separators and resolve dot segments with string operations. Brute Force: Repeatedly replace duplicated separators and resolve dot segments with string operations.
optimized: Split/scan path components. Ignore empty/. parts, pop on .., and push normal directory names onto a stack.

title: Min Stack
description: Design a stack supporting push, pop, top, and minimum retrieval in O(1).
example: push(-2), push(0), push(-3) getMin() -> -3 pop() top() -> 0 getMin() -> -2
brute: Use a normal stack and scan all elements whenever minimum is requested.
optimized: Store the current minimum alongside every pushed value, or maintain a second min stack.
bruteCost: Time O(n) for getMin | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(1) for all operations | Space O(n)

title: Asteroid Collision
description: Positive asteroids move right, negative asteroids move left. Simulate collisions where the smaller asteroid is destroyed.
brute: Repeatedly scan adjacent opposite-moving pairs and resolve collisions until stable.
optimized: Keep surviving asteroids in a stack. Only a positive stack top and a negative current asteroid can collide; resolve repeatedl y until one survives.

title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String II
description: Repeatedly remove groups of exactly k adjacent equal characters until no more such groups remain.
brute: Repeatedly scan the whole string and remove every length-k repeated group.
optimized: Maintain a stack of (character,count). Increment the top count for equal characters and remove the group when count reaches k.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) or worse | Space O(n)

title: Implement Stack Using Queues
description: Implement LIFO stack operations using only queue operations.
brute: Use two queues and move elements between them on every pop/top.
optimized: Use one queue; after each push, rotate previous elements behind the new element so the newest item remains at the front.
bruteCost: Time O(n) for pop/top | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) push, O(1) pop/top | Space O(n)

title: Implement Queue Using Stacks
description: Implement FIFO queue operations using only stacks.
