brute: On every pop, move all elements to a second stack, remove one, then move them back.
optimized: Use an input stack and output stack. Move elements from input to output only when output is empty.
bruteCost: Time O(n) per pop | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(1) amortized per operation | Space O(n)

title: Next Greater Element I
description: For each queried value from one array, return the first greater value to its right in a larger array.
brute: For every queried value, locate it and scan right until finding a greater value.
optimized: Scan nums2 with a decreasing stack. When the current value is greater than the stack top, it is that value's next greater element; store results in a map.
bruteCost: Time O(mn) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Daily Temperatures
description: For each day, return how many days until a warmer temperature, or 0 if none exists.
brute: For each day, scan forward for the first warmer day.
optimized: Keep indexes in a decreasing temperature stack. A warmer current day resolves all smaller temperatures on top.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Online Stock Span
description: For each new stock price, return how many consecutive days up to today had prices less than or equal to today's price.
brute: For every new price, scan backward while earlier prices are <= current.
optimized: Keep a decreasing stack of (price,span). Pop smaller/equal prices and add their spans to the current span.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) across all calls | Space O(n) history
optimizedCost: Time O(1) amortized per call | Space O(n)

title: Stock Span Problem
description: Given all stock prices at once, return the span for every day.
brute: For every day, scan left until finding a greater price.
optimized: Maintain indexes of previous greater values in a decreasing stack. Span is i - previousGreaterIndex, or i+1 if none exists.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Remove K Digits
description: Remove exactly k digits from a numeric string to produce the smallest possible number.
brute: Try every way to remove k positions and choose the smallest result.
optimized: Maintain an increasing stack. While the current digit is smaller than the top and removals remain, pop the top. Remove extra digits from the end if necessary.

title: 132 Pattern
description: Determine whether there exist indexes i < j < k such that nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j].
brute: Try every triple.
optimized: Scan from right with a decreasing stack representing possible 3 values and maintain the best popped value as the possible 2.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description: Given bar heights of width 1, find the largest rectangular area that can be formed using consecutive bars.
brute: For every bar, expand left and right while neighboring bars are at least as tall; compute the area.
optimized: Use a monotonic increasing stack to find the previous smaller and next smaller boundary for each height. When a lower bar arr ives, pop taller bars and calculate their maximal width immediately.

title: Maximal Rectangle
description: In a binary matrix, find the largest rectangle containing only 1s.
brute: Enumerate every possible rectangle and check whether all cells are 1.
optimized: Treat every matrix row as the base of a histogram. Update consecutive-1 heights column by column, then solve Largest Rectangle in Histogram for each row.
bruteCost: Time O(rows² × cols² × area) in a very naive solution | Space O(1)

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description: Return the kth largest array value.
brute: Sort descending and return index k-1.
optimized: Maintain a min-heap of size k; values larger than the heap minimum replace it. The heap top is the kth largest. QuickSelect gives O(n) average as an alternative.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space depends on sort
optimizedCost: Time O(n log k) | Space O(k)

title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
description: After each new streamed value, return the kth largest value seen so far.
brute: Store all values and sort after every insertion.
optimized: Keep only the largest k values in a min-heap. The heap top is always the kth largest.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) per add | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(log k) per add | Space O(k)

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Return the k values occurring most frequently.
brute: Count frequencies, then sort all unique values by frequency.
optimized: Count frequencies, then maintain a min-heap of only k values, or use frequency buckets for O(n) time.
bruteCost: Time O(n + u log u) | Space O(u)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log k) with heap | Space O(u)

title: Top K Frequent Words
description: Return the k most frequent words, breaking frequency ties by lexicographically smaller word first.
brute: Count frequencies and sort all unique words using frequency and lexical order.
optimized: Maintain a size-k heap with a comparator that treats lower frequency and lexicographically larger words as worse.
bruteCost: Time O(n + u log u) | Space O(u)
optimizedCost: Time O(n + u log k) | Space O(u + k)

title: K Closest Points to Origin
description: Return the k points with the smallest Euclidean distance from (0,0).
brute: Calculate all squared distances, sort points by distance, and take first k.
optimized: Maintain a max-heap of size k; remove the farthest point whenever size exceeds k.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n) depending on sort
optimizedCost: Time O(n log k) | Space O(k)

title: Sort Characters by Frequency
description: Rearrange characters so higher-frequency characters appear before lower-frequency characters.
brute: Count frequencies and sort all characters/entries by frequency.
optimized: Count characters, then use a max-heap or frequency buckets to output groups from highest frequency downward.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log u) with heap, O(n) with buckets | Space O(u+n)

title: Find Median From Data Stream
description: Support adding numbers and returning the median at any time.
brute: Store all values and sort whenever the median is requested.
optimized: Keep the smaller half in a max-heap and larger half in a min-heap; rebalance so their sizes differ by at most one.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) per median query | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(log n) add, O(1) median | Space O(n)

title: Merge K Sorted Lists
description: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list.
brute: Collect all values, sort them, and build a new list.
optimized: Put the current head of every non-empty list into a min-heap. Repeatedly remove the smallest node and insert its next node.
bruteCost: Time O(N log N) | Space O(N)
optimizedCost: Time O(N log k) | Space O(k)

title: Find K Pairs With Smallest Sums
description: From two sorted arrays, return k pairs with the smallest sums.
brute: Generate every pair, sort by sum, and take first k.
optimized: Start with pairs (nums1[i], nums2[0]) for limited i. Pop the smallest pair and push the next pair from the same row.
optimizedCost: Time O(k log min(k,m)) | Space O(min(k,m))

title: Find Kth Smallest Sum of Matrix With Sorted Rows
description: Choose one element from each sorted row. Return the kth smallest possible total sum.
brute: Generate every combination of one value per row, compute all sums, sort them.
optimized: Repeatedly merge the current list of smallest sums with the next row using a min-heap, keeping only the smallest k sums after each merge.
bruteCost: Time Exponential in number of rows | Space exponential
optimizedCost: Time roughly O(rows × k log k) | Space O(k)

title: Task Scheduler
description: Tasks with equal letters need at least n cooldown intervals between executions. Return the minimum total intervals.
brute: Simulate every valid choice of task order.
optimized: Either use the frequency formula based on the most frequent tasks or simulate with a max-heap plus cooldown queue.
optimizedCost: Time O(number of tasks) for the formula, or O(T log U) heap simulation | Space O(U)

title: Single Threaded CPU
description: Jobs have enqueue times and processing times. A single CPU chooses the available job with shortest processing time, then smallest index. Return execution order.
brute: At each time, scan all unfinished jobs to find eligible jobs and choose the best one.
optimized: Sort jobs by enqueue time and push available jobs into a min-heap ordered by processing time then index.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Reorganize String
description: Rearrange a string so no two adjacent characters are the same, or return empty if impossible.
brute: Try permutations until finding a valid one.
optimized: Use a max-heap of character frequencies. Repeatedly choose the most frequent character that is different from the immediately previous one.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log alphabet) | Space O(alphabet)

title: Rearrange String K Distance Apart
description: Rearrange characters so identical characters are at least k positions apart, or return empty if impossible.
brute: Try permutations and validate distance constraints.
optimized: Use a max-heap for available characters and a cooldown queue that releases a used character after k positions.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log alphabet) | Space O(alphabet + k)

title: Factorial
brute: Multiply values from 1..n iteratively.
optimized: Use factorial(n) = n × factorial(n-1) with base case factorial(0)=1.

title: Fibonacci
description: Return the nth Fibonacci number.
brute: Use direct recursion fib(n)=fib(n-1)+fib(n-2).
optimized: Keep only the previous two Fibonacci values and build upward.

title: Power of Three
description: Check whether an integer is an exact power of 3.
brute: Repeatedly divide by 3 while divisible.
optimized: For 32-bit signed integers, the largest power of three can be precomputed; n is a power of three if it is positive and divides that maximum power exactly.

title: Count Good Numbers
description: Count length-n digit strings where even indexes use even digits and odd indexes use prime digits, modulo a large constant.
brute: Generate every length-n digit string and test the position rules.
optimized: There are 5 choices for even positions and 4 choices for odd positions. Compute 5^ceil(n/2) × 4^floor(n/2) using fast exponentiation.
optimizedCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(1) iterative

title: Tower of Hanoi
description: Move n disks from source to destination using one auxiliary rod, never placing a larger disk on a smaller one.
brute: Move n-1 disks to auxiliary, move the largest disk to destination, then move n-1 disks onto it.
optimized: The minimum number of moves is inherently 2^n - 1; no asymptotically faster algorithm can output all moves.

title: Josephus Problem
description: n people stand in a circle and every kth person is eliminated. Return the winner.
brute: Store people in a list and repeatedly remove every kth person.
optimized: Use the recurrence winner(1)=0, winner(n)=(winner(n-1)+k)%n, then convert to 1-based indexing.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) with array/list removals | Space O(n)

title: Integer to English Words
description: Convert a non-negative integer into English words.
example: Example: Input: 12345 Output: "Twelve Thousand Three Hundred Forty Five"
brute: Handle every numeric range with many repeated condition branches.
optimized: Recursively convert reusable chunks below 1000, then process billions, millions, thousands, and remainder using the same helper.
bruteCost: Time O(number of digits) | Space O(number of digits) output
optimizedCost: Time O(number of digits) | Space O(number of digits) recursion/output

title: Subsets
description: Return every subset of a set of distinct integers.
brute: Use a bitmask from 0 to 2^n-1 and build the subset for every mask.
optimized: At each index make two choices: take the element or skip it.
bruteCost: Time O(n × 2^n) | Space O(1) excluding output
optimizedCost: Time O(n × 2^n) including output copying | Space O(n) recursion

title: Subsets II
description: Return all unique subsets when the input can contain duplicates.
brute: Generate all subsets and put them into a set to remove duplicates.
optimized: Sort first. During backtracking, skip equal choices at the same recursion level.
bruteCost: Time O(n × 2^n) plus set/hash overhead | Space O(2^n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n × 2^n) output bound | Space O(n) recursion excluding output

title: Permutations
description: Return all permutations of distinct numbers.
brute: Generate every ordering by swapping/choosing unused elements; this is already the natural exhaustive approach.
optimized: At each position, swap in each remaining value, recurse, then undo the swap. Each completed path produces one permutation.
bruteCost: Time O(n × n!) | Space O(n) recursion

title: Permutations II
description: Return all unique permutations when input values can repeat.
brute: Generate all permutations and deduplicate with a set.
optimized: Sort input and skip a duplicate value when the previous equal value has not been used in the current construction path.
bruteCost: Time O(n × n!) | Space very large
optimizedCost: Time O(number of unique permutations × n) | Space O(n) recursion/used array

title: Combinations
description: Return all ways to choose k numbers from 1..n.
brute: Generate all subsets and keep only those of size k.
optimized: Backtrack with a start index and choose only remaining values; stop once the current combination has size k.
optimizedCost: Time O(C(n,k) × k) | Space O(k) recursion

title: Combination Sum
description: Return combinations of candidate values that sum to target; each candidate may be reused unlimited times.
brute: Recursively try every candidate repeatedly without pruning.
optimized: Backtrack from a start index, reuse the current candidate, stop when remaining target becomes negative, and record when it re aches zero.
bruteCost: Time Exponential | Space proportional to target depth
optimizedCost: Time Exponential, but strongly pruned | Space O(target/minCandidate) recursion

title: Combination Sum II
description: Return unique combinations summing to target where each input element can be used at most once.
brute: Generate subsets and filter sums, using a set to remove duplicates.
optimized: Sort, choose each index at most once, and skip equal values at the same recursion level.
optimizedCost: Time Exponential but pruned | Space O(n) recursion

title: Combination Sum III
description: Choose exactly k distinct numbers from 1..9 whose sum is n.
brute: Generate all subsets of 1..9 and filter by size and sum.
optimized: Backtrack from a start number while tracking remaining count and remaining sum; prune impossible branches.
optimizedCost: Time small combinational search | Space O(k)

title: Letter Combinations of Phone Number
description: Given digits 2..9, return all letter combinations represented by telephone keypad mappings.
brute: Build combinations by repeatedly forming a new list for every digit.
optimized: Backtrack one digit at a time, choosing each mapped letter and undoing after recursion.
bruteCost: Time O(4^n × n) worst case | Space O(4^n × n)
optimizedCost: Time O(4^n × n) output bound | Space O(n) recursion excluding output

title: Generate Parentheses
description: Return all valid strings containing n pairs of parentheses.
brute: Generate all 2^(2n) strings of ( and ) and validate each.
optimized: Backtrack only valid prefixes: add ( while open count < n; add ) only when close count < open count.
optimizedCost: Time proportional to Catalan-number output | Space O(n) recursion

title: N-Queens
description: Place n queens on an n×n board so no two queens attack each other. Return all valid boards.
brute: Try placing queens in arbitrary cells and validate whole boards.
optimized: Place exactly one queen per row and track occupied columns, main diagonals, and anti-diagonals in sets/boolean arrays.
bruteCost: Time extremely high, roughly O((n² choose n) × validation) | Space board dependent
optimizedCost: Time about O(n!) search | Space O(n) excluding output

title: N-Queens II
description: Return only the number of valid N-Queens arrangements.
brute: Generate placements and validate them after completion.
optimized: Row-by-row backtracking with column and diagonal occupancy; increment count whenever all rows are placed.
bruteCost: Time extremely high | Space board dependent

title: Sudoku Solver
description: Fill empty cells in a 9×9 Sudoku so every row, column, and 3×3 box contains digits 1..9 exactly once.
example: Input: partially filled valid Sudoku Output: completed Sudoku board
brute: For every empty cell, try all digits and validate the whole board repeatedly.
optimized: Track used digits per row, column, and box so validity checks are O(1); backtrack only valid choices.
bruteCost: Time exponential, up to O(9^E) for E empty cells | Space O(E) recursion
optimizedCost: Time exponential worst case but much more pruned | Space O(E + 9²)

title: Word Search
description: Determine whether a word can be formed by adjacent horizontal/vertical cells without reusing a cell.
brute: Generate many paths from every cell without strong pruning.
optimized: Start DFS only from matching first letters; mark a cell temporarily visited, explore matching next letters, then restore it.
bruteCost: Time up to O(rows × cols × 4^L) | Space O(L)
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols × 4^L) worst case | Space O(L) recursion

title: Rat in a Maze
description: Return valid paths from the top-left to bottom-right of a grid where blocked cells cannot be entered.
example: Input: binary maze Output: paths such as "DDRDRR"
brute: Explore all movement sequences, including invalid/repeated positions.
optimized: Backtrack only through valid unvisited cells, mark visited during the current path, and undo when returning.
optimizedCost: Time exponential in open cells | Space O(rows × cols) visited/path

title: Unique Paths III
description: Count paths from start to end that walk over every non-obstacle square exactly once.
brute: Explore all four-direction paths and separately verify whether all required cells were visited.
optimized: Count walkable cells first. During backtracking decrement remaining cells; count a path only when reaching the end with exact ly all required cells consumed.

title: Palindrome Partitioning
description: Return all ways to partition a string so every piece is a palindrome.
brute: Generate all 2^(n-1) possible cut combinations and validate every produced substring.
optimized: At each start index, try only prefixes that are palindromes; recurse from the next position immediately.
bruteCost: Time roughly O(2^n × n²) | Space O(n) recursion
optimizedCost: Time exponential output-dependent | Space O(n) recursion

title: Restore IP Addresses
description: Insert three dots into a digit string to form all valid IPv4 addresses.
brute: Try all dot positions and validate the resulting four segments.
optimized: Backtrack exactly four segments, each of length 1..3, pruning leading zeroes and values over 255 immediately.
bruteCost: Time O(n³) combinations of cuts | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time effectively O(1) bounded search for IPv4 lengths | Space O(4) recursion

title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
description: Determine whether the array can be divided into k non-empty subsets with equal sums.
brute: Assign every element to one of k buckets in all possible ways.
optimized: If total sum is divisible by k, sort descending and backtrack filling buckets toward the target sum, pruning symmetric/overflow states.
optimizedCost: Time exponential worst case | Space O(k+n)

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Return node values level by level from top to bottom.
brute: Compute tree height, then recursively collect nodes for level 1, level 2, and so on.
optimized: Use a queue. For each level, process exactly the current queue size before moving to the next level.
bruteCost: Time O(nh) worst case O(n²) | Space O(h) recursion

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal II
description: Return level-order traversal from bottom level to top.
brute: Normal level order, then reverse the result list.
optimized: Perform BFS and add each completed level to the front of a linked result structure.

title: N-ary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Return the values of an N-ary tree level by level.
example: Input: N-ary tree rooted at 1 Output: [[1],[3,2,4],[5,6]]
brute: Recursively collect nodes separately for every depth.
optimized: BFS with a queue; enqueue all children of each processed node.

title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
description: Return level order, alternating left-to-right and right-to-left at each level.
brute: Run normal BFS, then reverse every second level.
optimized: During BFS, insert each level's value at the end or front depending on the current direction.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(width) excluding output

title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description: Return the nodes visible when viewing a binary tree from the right side.
brute: Build full level order and take the last value of each level.
optimized: BFS and record only the final node processed at every level, or DFS right-first and record the first node at each depth.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(width) BFS or O(h) DFS

title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
description: Return the average node value for every tree level.
brute: Gather all level values first, then calculate averages.
optimized: During BFS, maintain one sum and count for the current level and immediately append its average.

title: Cousins in Binary Tree
description: Determine whether two nodes are at the same depth but have different parents.
example: Input: tree=[1,2,3,4], x=4, y=3 Output: false
brute: Separately find depth and parent of each target using full traversals.
optimized: BFS level by level; when targets appear on the same level, ensure they are not children of the same parent.
bruteCost: Time O(n) but multiple passes | Space O(h)

title: Binary Tree Preorder Traversal
description: Return nodes in root -> left -> right order.
brute: Visit root, recurse left, recurse right.
optimized: Use a stack; push right child before left child so left is processed first.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(h) to O(n)

title: N-ary Tree Preorder Traversal
description: Return N-ary tree nodes in root-first preorder.
example: Input: N-ary tree rooted at 1 Output: preorder values
brute: Visit node, then recursively visit each child from left to right.
optimized: Use a stack and push children in reverse order.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(n) worst case

title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
description: Return nodes in left -> root -> right order.
brute: Recurse left, visit root, recurse right.
optimized: Push the left chain to a stack, pop a node, then move to its right subtree.

title: Binary Tree Postorder Traversal
description: Return nodes in left -> right -> root order.
brute: Recurse left, recurse right, then visit root.
optimized: Use one/two stacks, or process root-right-left then reverse the output.

title: N-ary Tree Postorder Traversal
description: Return an N-ary tree in children-first, root-last order.
example: Input: N-ary tree Output: postorder values
brute: Recursively visit every child, then the current node.
optimized: Use a stack to generate root-first reverse order, then reverse the result.

title: Height of Binary Tree
description: Return the number of levels/nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path, according to the chosen height convention.
brute: BFS level order and count how many levels are processed.
optimized: height(node) = 1 + max(height(left), height(right)).

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Return the maximum number of nodes from root to any leaf.
brute: BFS level by level and count levels.
optimized: Return 1 + max(leftDepth,rightDepth) recursively.

title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Return the shortest root-to-leaf depth.
brute: DFS every root-to-leaf path and track minimum depth.
optimized: BFS; the first leaf encountered is automatically at minimum depth.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) worst case, often stops earlier | Space O(width)

title: Maximum Depth of N-ary Tree
description: Return the maximum depth of an N-ary tree.
example: Input: N-ary tree Output: longest root-to-leaf level count
brute: BFS and count levels.
optimized: For each node return 1 + max(depth(child)) over all children.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
description: Return the maximum number of edges on any path between two tree nodes.
brute: For every node, separately compute left height and right height, causing repeated subtree work.
optimized: Postorder DFS returns subtree height while updating global diameter with leftHeight + rightHeight at each node.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) worst case | Space O(h)

title: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
description: Return the maximum width between the leftmost and rightmost non-null nodes at any level, counting null gaps between them.
brute: Materialize null positions level by level, which can grow exponentially.
optimized: BFS with conceptual complete-tree indexes. Width is lastIndex - firstIndex + 1; normalize indexes per level to prevent overflow.
bruteCost: Time potentially very large | Space potentially very large

title: Same Tree
description: Determine whether two binary trees have identical structure and values.
brute: Serialize both trees completely and compare serialized strings.
optimized: Recursively compare corresponding nodes; both null is equal, one null/value mismatch is false.

title: Symmetric Tree
description: Determine whether a binary tree is a mirror of itself around its center.
brute: Invert one subtree into a copy and compare it with the other subtree.
optimized: Recursively compare left.left with right.right and left.right with right.left.

title: Balanced Binary Tree
description: Determine whether every node's left and right subtree heights differ by at most one.
brute: At every node, call a separate height function for both subtrees.
optimized: Postorder DFS returns height, but returns a failure marker immediately when a subtree is unbalanced.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) worst case | Space O(h)

title: Subtree of Another Tree
description: Determine whether subRoot appears as an exact subtree inside another tree.
brute: At every root node, run a full same-tree comparison with subRoot.
optimized: Still commonly DFS each candidate root plus same-tree check; serialization with separators and string matching can reduce repeated structural comparisons in some implementati ons.
bruteCost: Time O(nm) worst case | Space O(h)
optimizedCost: Time typically O(nm), or near O(n+m) with robust serialization + linear matching | Space O(n+m) for serialization approach

title: Left View of Binary Tree
description: Return the first visible node at every level when the tree is viewed from the left.
brute: Build every level and take its first value.
optimized: DFS left-first and record the first node encountered at each depth.

title: Top View of Binary Tree
description: Return nodes visible from above, one for each horizontal distance from the root.
example: Input: binary tree Output: top-view values from left to right
brute: Collect every node with horizontal distance and depth, then sort/group and choose minimum depth.
optimized: BFS with (node,horizontalDistance) and store only the first node seen at each horizontal distance.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) with ordered map, O(n) average with hash map plus range tracking | Space O(n)

title: Bottom View of Binary Tree
description: Return nodes visible from below, one for each horizontal distance.
example: Input: binary tree Output: bottom-view values
brute: Collect all nodes with horizontal distance and depth, then choose the deepest per distance.
optimized: BFS and overwrite the stored node for each horizontal distance; later nodes at the same distance are deeper/equally deep.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) with ordered map | Space O(n)

title: Find Bottom Left Tree Value
description: Return the leftmost value in the last tree row.
brute: Store all level-order rows and take the first value of the final row.
optimized: BFS level by level while remembering the first node at each level; final remembered value is the answer.

title: Boundary Traversal
description: Return root, left boundary, leaves, and right boundary in anti-clockwise order without duplicates.
example: Input: binary tree Output: anti-clockwise boundary values Output: anti-clockwise boundary values
brute: Collect many root-to-leaf paths and derive boundary nodes afterward.
optimized: Separately add non-leaf left boundary, all leaves, and non-leaf right boundary in reverse order.
bruteCost: Time higher than needed | Space high
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(h) recursion excluding output

title: Vertical Order Traversal
description: Group nodes by vertical column, ordered by column and then required row/value rules.
brute: Store (column,row,value) for every node and sort all records globally.
optimized: BFS/DFS while grouping by column and row; use ordered maps/heaps as needed by the exact tie-breaking rule.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Path Sum
description: Determine whether any root-to-leaf path sums to a target.
brute: Generate every root-to-leaf path, store its values, then calculate its sum.
optimized: DFS while subtracting each node value from the remaining target; at a leaf, check whether remaining target equals the leaf va lue.
bruteCost: Time O(nh) due to copying/summing paths | Space O(nh) worst case

title: Path Sum II
description: Return all root-to-leaf paths whose values sum to the target.
example: Input: target=22 Output: paths such as [5,4,11,2]
brute: Generate all root-to-leaf paths first, then filter by sum.
optimized: Backtrack with a running path and remaining target; copy the current path only when reaching a valid leaf.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) traversal plus output copying | Space O(h) excluding output

title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
description: Each root-to-leaf path forms a base-10 number. Return the sum of all such numbers.
brute: Build each path as a string/list, convert it to a number at leaves, and sum.
optimized: Carry the numeric prefix directly: current = current*10 + node.val; add it when a leaf is reached.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: Find the maximum sum of any non-empty path in a binary tree; the path may start and end anywhere.
brute: Consider every node as a path center and repeatedly calculate best downward paths in both subtrees.
optimized: Postorder DFS returns the best downward gain from each node. Update global answer with node + max(0,leftGain) + max(0,rightGain).
bruteCost: Time O(n²) worst case | Space O(h)

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of Binary Tree
description: Return the lowest node that is an ancestor of both target nodes in a general binary tree.
brute: Build ancestor paths from root to each target, then compare both paths until they diverge.
optimized: DFS: if current node is p or q, return it. If left and right both return non-null, current node is the LCA; otherwise return the non-null side.

title: Construct Binary Tree From Preorder + Inorder
description: Rebuild a binary tree from preorder and inorder traversals with unique values.
brute: Choose preorder root, linearly search it in inorder, copy left/right subarrays, and recurse.
optimized: Store value -> inorder index in a hash map and pass index boundaries through recursion instead of copying arrays.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n²) with repeated array copies

title: Construct Binary Tree From Inorder + Postorder
description: Rebuild a tree from inorder and postorder traversals.
brute: Take the last postorder value as root, search it in inorder, copy subarrays, recurse.
optimized: Use an inorder index map and a moving postorder pointer from right to left; build the right subtree before the left subtree.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space high with copying

title: Construct String From Binary Tree
description: Build a parenthesized preorder string representation while omitting unnecessary empty parentheses.
brute: Serialize all null children explicitly, then repeatedly remove unnecessary empty markers.
optimized: Preorder DFS and add parentheses only according to the rules: include empty left () only when a right child exists without a left child.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) possible string rewriting | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(h) recursion plus output

title: Invert Binary Tree
description: Mirror a binary tree by swapping every node's left and right children.
brute: Build a separate mirrored copy of the tree. Brute Force: Build a separate mirrored copy of the tree.
optimized: At every node swap left/right pointers in place and recursively or iteratively process children.
bruteCost: Time O(n) | Space O(n) new nodes
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(h) recursion or O(width) queue

title: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
description: Flatten a binary tree in place into a right-only linked list following preorder traversal.
brute: Collect preorder nodes in a list, then reconnect them sequentially.
optimized: For each node with a left subtree, find the rightmost node of that subtree, attach the original right subtree there, move lef t subtree to right, and clear left.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) amortized with Morris-style rewiring | Space O(1)

title: Merge Two Binary Trees
description: Merge two trees by summing overlapping nodes; non-overlapping nodes remain unchanged.
example: Input: two binary trees Output: merged tree with summed overlaps
brute: Create an entirely new tree while recursively examining both inputs.
optimized: Reuse one tree: where both nodes exist, add values and recursively merge children; where one is null, return the other subtre e directly.
bruteCost: Time O(n+m) | Space O(n+m) new nodes
optimizedCost: Time O(min-overlap plus visited nodes) | Space O(h) recursion

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description: Convert a binary tree into a string and reconstruct the exact same tree from that string.
example: Input tree: [1,2,3,null,null,4,5] Serialized: implementation-specific string Deserialized: same tree
brute: Store a verbose object-like representation with many structural markers.
optimized: Use preorder or level-order traversal with explicit null markers so structure is unambiguous; deserialize by consuming tokens in the same order.

title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node II
description: Connect each node's next pointer to the next node on the same level in an arbitrary binary tree.
example: Input: [1,2,3,4,5,null,7] Output: next pointers connect each level left-to-right
brute: BFS with a queue and connect consecutive nodes at every level.
optimized: Traverse each existing level through already-built next pointers while constructing the next level with a dummy head and tail pointer.

title: Count Complete Tree Nodes
description: Count nodes in a complete binary tree faster than visiting every node.
brute: DFS/BFS and count every node.
optimized: Compare leftmost and rightmost heights. If equal, the subtree is perfect and has 2^h - 1 nodes; otherwise recurse into children.
bruteCost: Time O(n) | Space O(h) or O(width)
optimizedCost: Time O(log² n) | Space O(log n)

title: Count Leaves in Binary Tree
description: Return the number of nodes having no left or right child.
brute: BFS all nodes and count nodes with no children.
optimized: Return 1 for a leaf and recursively sum leaf counts from left and right children.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Determine whether every node satisfies the global BST ordering rules.
brute: For every node, repeatedly find maximum in its left subtree and minimum in its right subtree.
optimized: DFS with an allowed (lower, upper) range for each node, or verify inorder traversal is strictly increasing.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) worst case | Space O(h)

title: Kth Smallest Element in BST
description: Return the kth smallest value in a BST.
brute: Collect all values, sort them, and return index k-1.
optimized: BST inorder traversal is sorted; stop when the kth node is visited.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(h+k) average / O(n) worst case | Space O(h)

title: Inorder Successor in BST
description: Return the smallest BST value greater than a target node/value.
brute: Perform full inorder traversal and find the value immediately after target.
optimized: Starting from root, whenever current value is greater than target, store it as a candidate and move left; otherwise move right.

title: Minimum Absolute Difference in BST
description: Return the minimum absolute difference between values of any two BST nodes.
brute: Collect all node values and compare every pair.
optimized: Inorder traversal gives sorted values, so only adjacent inorder values need comparison.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of BST
description: Return the lowest node that is an ancestor of two target nodes in a BST.
brute: Build root-to-node paths for both targets and compare them.
optimized: If both target values are smaller, move left; if both are larger, move right; otherwise current node is the split point/LCA.
bruteCost: Time O(h) plus stored paths | Space O(h)

title: Binary Search Tree Iterator
description: Design an iterator returning BST values in ascending order with next() and hasNext().
brute: Precompute full inorder traversal into an array.
optimized: Store only the current left spine in a stack. After returning a node, push the left spine of its right subtree.
bruteCost: Time O(n) initialization, O(1) next | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(1) amortized next | Space O(h)

title: Convert Sorted Array to BST
description: Convert an ascending array into a height-balanced BST.
brute: Insert values one by one into a BST; depending on order this may not stay balanced.
optimized: Recursively choose the middle array element as root, then build left/right halves the same way.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) average | Space O(h)
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(log n) recursion

title: Convert BST to Greater Tree
description: Replace each BST node value with its original value plus the sum of all greater values.
example: Input BST: [4,1,6,...] Output: transformed greater tree
brute: For every node, traverse the tree to sum all greater values.
optimized: Reverse inorder traversal (right -> root -> left) visits values from largest to smallest; maintain a running sum.

title: Trim a BST
description: Remove nodes whose values fall outside [low,high] while preserving BST structure.
brute: Traverse all nodes and rebuild a new BST using only allowed values.
optimized: If node value is below low, discard node and its entire left subtree; if above high, discard node and its entire right subtree; otherwise trim both children.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) average | Space O(n)

title: Convert BST to Sorted Doubly Linked List
description: Convert a BST into a sorted circular doubly linked list in place.
example: Input BST: 2 with children 1 and 3 Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 <-> back to 1
brute: Inorder-traverse into an array, then link adjacent nodes afterward.
optimized: During inorder traversal, connect each current node directly with the previous visited node; finally connect head and tail.

title: Unique Binary Search Trees
description: Return how many structurally unique BSTs can store values 1..n.
brute: Recursively choose every possible root and independently compute left/right tree counts without memoization.
optimized: Dynamic programming with Catalan recurrence: dp[n] = Σ dp[leftSize] × dp[rightSize].

title: Implement Trie - Prefix Tree
description: Implement insert, exact search, and startsWith for lowercase words.
example: insert("apple") search("apple") -> true search("app") -> false startsWith("app") -> true
brute: Store all words in a list; scan every stored word for each search/prefix query.
optimized: Store one trie node per character path. Exact search follows characters and checks end-of-word; prefix search only needs the path to exist.
bruteCost: Time O(numberWords × wordLength) per query | Space O(total characters)
optimizedCost: Time O(wordLength) per operation | Space O(total inserted characters)

title: Design Add and Search Words
description: Store words and support searches where . can match any one character.
brute: Store words in a list and compare the pattern with every word character by character.
optimized: Use a trie. Normal characters follow one child; . recursively explores every child at that trie position.
bruteCost: Time O(numberWords × wordLength) | Space O(total characters)
optimizedCost: Time O(L) without wildcards, potentially branching exponentially with many . | Space O(total inserted characters)

title: Word Search II
description: Given a character board and a list of words, return all words that can be formed by adjacent cells without cell reuse.
brute: Run the full Word Search DFS independently for every word.
optimized: Put all words into one trie. Start DFS from board cells and follow trie prefixes; abandon paths that are not prefixes of any word.
bruteCost: Time roughly O(words × rows × cols × 4^L) | Space recursion plus word storage
optimizedCost: Time greatly pruned; worst case still exponential in path length | Space O(total word characters + board path)

title: Clone Graph
description: Deep-copy a connected graph where each node contains a value and neighbor list.
example: Input: adjacency list [[2,4],[1,3],[2,4],[1,3]] Output: independent graph with same structure
brute: Create nodes while traversing but without a map, which causes repeated copies and cannot correctly handle cycles.
optimized: DFS/BFS with a map originalNode -> copiedNode. Create each node once and connect copied neighbors.

title: Number of Islands
description: Count connected groups of land cells (1) in a grid using horizontal/vertical adjacency.
brute: For each land cell, repeatedly search the grid to determine which island it belongs to.
optimized: Scan the grid; whenever unvisited land is found, increment island count and DFS/BFS to mark its entire component visited.
bruteCost: Time much higher than O(rc) | Space high depending on grouping
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols) | Space O(rows × cols) worst-case recursion/queue

title: Max Area of Island
description: Return the maximum number of cells in any connected island.
example: Input: binary grid Output: largest connected land-cell count
brute: From every land cell, explore its island independently without preserving visited state.
optimized: DFS/BFS each island once, mark cells visited, and return the component size.
bruteCost: Time O((rc)²) worst case | Space O(rc)
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols) | Space O(rows × cols) worst case

title: Flood Fill
description: Starting from one image cell, recolor all 4-direction-connected cells having the same original color.
brute: Repeatedly scan the whole image for cells connected to the source color.
optimized: DFS/BFS from the start and recolor only cells matching the original color.
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols) worst case | Space O(rows × cols) worst case

title: Surrounded Regions
description: Flip O regions completely surrounded by X; Os connected to the border must remain unchanged.
example: Input: XXXX XOOX XXOX XOXX Output: XXXX XXXX XXXX XOXX
brute: For every O, run a search to see whether its region touches a border.
optimized: Start DFS/BFS from border Os and mark them safe. Then flip every remaining O and restore safe markers.
bruteCost: Time O((rc)²) worst case | Space O(rc)
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols) | Space O(rows × cols) worst case

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
description: Return cells from which water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, where water moves to equal/lower heights.
example: Input: height matrix Output: coordinates able to reach both oceans
brute: From every cell, DFS downhill to check whether both oceans can be reached.
optimized: Reverse the problem. DFS/BFS inward from Pacific borders and Atlantic borders, moving only to equal/higher cells. Intersection of reachable sets is the answer.
bruteCost: Time O((rc)²) worst case | Space O(rc)
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols) | Space O(rows × cols)

title: Time Needed to Inform All Employees
description: A manager hierarchy forms a tree. Return the total time needed for the head to inform every employee.
example: Input: manager hierarchy + informTime Output: maximum time from head to any employee
brute: For every employee, walk upward through managers to calculate total time from the head.
optimized: Build manager-to-subordinates adjacency and DFS/BFS from the head while accumulating elapsed time; take the maximum.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) worst case | Space O(1) extra

title: Word Ladder
description: Transform beginWord to endWord by changing one letter at a time, with every intermediate word in the dictionary. Return minimum sequence length.
brute: Build all possible transformation sequences with DFS and take the shortest.
optimized: Treat each word as a graph node and run BFS, generating one-letter neighbors; the first time end word is reached gives shortest transformation length. Optimized: Treat each word as a graph node and run BFS, generating one-letter neighbors; the first time end word is reached gives shortest transformation length.
optimizedCost: Time roughly O(N × L × alphabet) | Space O(N)

title: Snakes and Ladders
description: On a numbered board with snakes/ladders, return the minimum dice throws needed to reach the final square.
example: Input: snakes/ladders board Output: minimum moves
brute: Explore all possible dice sequences with DFS.
optimized: Model each square as a graph node with up to six outgoing dice moves, applying snake/ladder jumps, then run BFS.
optimizedCost: Time O(board cells) | Space O(board cells)

title: Minimum Genetic Mutation
description: Change one gene character at a time to transform start gene into end gene, using only genes from the bank. Return minimum mutations.
brute: DFS through all mutation sequences.
optimized: BFS over valid gene strings; each mutation changes one position to one of A,C,G,T.

title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
description: In an n×n binary grid, find the shortest 8-direction path from top-left to bottom-right through zero cells.
brute: DFS every possible path and keep the minimum length.
optimized: BFS from the start because every move has equal cost; the first time the destination is reached is shortest.

title: Rotting Oranges
description: Each minute, rotten oranges rot adjacent fresh oranges. Return minutes until all fresh oranges rot, or -1.
brute: Minute by minute, scan the entire grid to find fresh oranges adjacent to rotten ones.
optimized: Put all initially rotten oranges into one queue and run multi-source BFS level by level.
bruteCost: Time O(minutes × rows × cols) | Space O(rows × cols) for changes
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols) | Space O(rows × cols)

title: 01 Matrix
description: For each cell, return the distance to the nearest 0.
brute: Run BFS from every 1 cell until reaching a 0.
optimized: Start BFS simultaneously from all 0 cells; the first distance assigned to each 1 is its nearest-zero distance.
bruteCost: Time O((rc)²) worst case | Space O(rc)
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols) | Space O(rows × cols)

title: Walls and Gates
description: Fill each empty room with its distance to the nearest gate; walls block movement.
example: Input: grid with INF rooms, -1 walls, 0 gates Output: each room replaced by nearest-gate distance
brute: BFS separately from every empty room searching for a gate.
optimized: Put all gates into the queue initially and run multi-source BFS outward into unfilled rooms.
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols) | Space O(rows × cols)

title: Number of Provinces
description: Given an adjacency matrix of cities, return the number of connected groups.
brute: Repeatedly rescan all matrix entries trying to merge known groups manually.
optimized: For each unvisited city, increment component count and DFS/BFS all cities reachable from it.
bruteCost: Time higher than necessary | Space high
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) for adjacency matrix | Space O(n)

title: Number of Connected Components in Undirected Graph
description: Given n nodes and undirected edges, return the number of connected components.
brute: Build reachability between every pair and group nodes afterward.
optimized: Build adjacency list and DFS/BFS from each unvisited node, or use Union Find while processing edges.
bruteCost: Time O(n³) with naive closure | Space O(n²)

title: Course Schedule
description: Determine whether all courses can be completed given prerequisite edges.
brute: Try possible course orderings and validate prerequisites.
optimized: Detect a cycle using Kahn's indegree BFS or DFS recursion-state coloring. All courses are possible iff no directed cycle exists.

title: Course Schedule II
description: Return a valid ordering of courses satisfying all prerequisites, or empty if impossible.
brute: Generate permutations until one satisfies all edges.
optimized: Kahn's topological sort: enqueue indegree-zero courses, remove them, decrement neighbors, and return the produced order if it contains all nodes.

title: Alien Dictionary
description: Given words sorted according to an unknown alphabet, derive one valid character order.
brute: Try character permutations and test which order makes all words sorted.
optimized: Compare adjacent words; the first differing characters create a directed edge. Topologically sort the character graph, also d etecting invalid prefix cases/cycles.
bruteCost: Time factorial in number of characters | Space large
optimizedCost: Time O(total characters + alphabet edges) | Space O(alphabet + edges)

title: Find Eventual Safe States
description: Return graph nodes from which every possible path eventually ends at a terminal node rather than a cycle.
brute: From each node independently explore all paths and check whether any path reaches a cycle.
optimized: DFS with states unvisited/visiting/safe, or reverse the graph and run Kahn's algorithm from terminal nodes.

title: Graph Valid Tree
description: Determine whether an undirected graph is exactly one tree.
brute: Check connectivity separately and try cycle detection with repeated traversals.
optimized: A tree must have exactly n-1 edges and be connected. DFS/BFS once, or use Union Find and reject any edge joining already -connected nodes.
bruteCost: Time higher than needed | Space O(V+E)
optimizedCost: Time O(V+E) | Space O(V+E) or O(V) with DSU

title: Redundant Connection
description: An undirected graph started as a tree and received one extra edge. Return the edge that created the cycle.
brute: Remove each edge and test whether the remaining graph is a tree.
optimized: Union Find each edge. The first/required edge whose endpoints already share the same root is redundant.

title: Accounts Merge
description: Merge accounts belonging to the same person when they share at least one email address.
example: Input: accounts with names and emails Output: merged accounts with sorted unique emails
brute: Repeatedly compare every account pair for shared emails and merge until stable.
optimized: Map every email to an owner/index and union accounts sharing emails. Group emails by final DSU root and sort each group.
bruteCost: Time roughly O(A² × E) | Space high
optimizedCost: Time near O(totalEmails α(A) + sorting) | Space O(totalEmails + A)

title: Is Graph Bipartite?
description: Determine whether graph nodes can be colored with two colors so every edge connects different colors.
brute: Try all 2^V color assignments and validate every edge.
optimized: BFS/DFS each component while assigning alternating colors; a conflict means not bipartite.

title: Evaluate Division
description: Equations such as a/b = 2.0 form weighted graph edges. Answer division queries between variables.
example: Equations: a/b=2, b/c=3 Query: a/c Output: 6.0
brute: For each query, try algebraically combining equations in many orders.
optimized: Build weighted edges a->b=value and b->a=1/value; DFS/BFS from query numerator to denominator while multiplying edge weights.
bruteCost: Time potentially very high | Space high
optimizedCost: Time O(V+E) per query | Space O(V+E)

title: Network Delay Time
description: Given directed positive-weight edges, return how long a signal from source k takes to reach all nodes, or -1 if some node is unreachable.
brute: Repeatedly relax all edges V-1 times using Bellman-Ford.
optimized: Use Dijkstra because weights are positive. The answer is the maximum finalized shortest distance if all nodes are reached.
optimizedCost: Time O((V+E) log V) | Space O(V+E)

title: Path With Minimum Effort
description: In a height grid, path effort is the maximum absolute height difference between adjacent cells. Minimize that maximum.
brute: Explore all possible paths and calculate each path's maximum edge difference.
optimized: Dijkstra where a cell's distance is the minimum possible maximum edge effort to reach it; relaxing an edge uses max(currentEffort, edgeDifference).

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
description: Find the cheapest flight cost from source to destination using at most k stops.
brute: DFS all routes up to k+1 edges and track minimum cost.
optimized: Bellman-Ford limited to k+1 relaxation rounds using a copy of previous distances so each round adds at most one edge.

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
description: Connect all 2D points with edges weighted by Manhattan distance so total connection cost is minimum.
brute: Generate all spanning trees and choose the minimum-cost one.
optimized: Build/consider weighted edges and run Prim's algorithm with a priority queue, or Kruskal with sorted edges and Union Find.
optimizedCost: Time O(E log V) Prim / O(E log E) Kruskal | Space O(E+V)

title: Fibonacci Number
description: Return the nth Fibonacci number.
brute: Direct recursion calls fib(n-1) and fib(n-2) repeatedly.
optimized: Build answers bottom-up while keeping only the previous two values.

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You may climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach step n.
brute: From each step recursively choose a jump of 1 or 2.
optimized: Ways to reach step i equal ways[i-1] + ways[i-2]; keep only two previous values.

title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
description: Each stair has a cost. You may climb one or two steps after paying a stair's cost. Return minimum cost to reach the top.
brute: Recursively try stepping one or two positions from each index.
optimized: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]); only the previous two states are required.

title: House Robber
description: Houses in a row contain money. You cannot rob adjacent houses. Return the maximum amount.
brute: At every house choose to rob it and skip the next, or skip it.
optimized: best[i] = max(best[i-1], nums[i] + best[i-2]); keep only the previous two states.

title: House Robber II
description: Houses form a circle, so the first and last houses are adjacent. Return maximum robbery amount.
brute: Recursively explore valid robbery subsets with circular adjacency rules.
optimized: A valid solution cannot take both first and last. Solve normal House Robber twice: [0..n-2] and [1..n-1], then take the maximum.

title: Decode Ways
description: Digits map 1->A ... 26->Z. Return the number of ways to decode a digit string.
brute: At each index recursively decode one digit and, when valid, two digits.
optimized: DP where ways at position i receive contributions from a valid one-digit code and a valid two-digit code.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(1) with rolling states

title: Frog Jump
description: A frog jumps across stones at given positions. Its next jump length may be previous jump -1, k, or k+1. Determine whether it can reach the last stone.
brute: DFS all possible jump lengths from every reachable stone.
optimized: Memoize state (stoneIndex,lastJump) or maintain a set of jump sizes that can reach each stone.
optimizedCost: Time about O(n²) worst case | Space O(n²)

title: Frog Jump II
description: Jump from first to last stone and back while visiting stones under the problem's constraints; minimize the maximum jump length.
brute: Explore assignments of stones to outward and return journeys.
optimized: The optimal route alternates stones; the answer is the maximum distance between stones two positions apart, also considering edge cases.

title: Subset Sum
description: Determine whether some subset sums exactly to a target.
brute: At each element choose take or skip.
optimized: Boolean DP where dp[s] means sum s is achievable. For 0/1 use, update sums backward.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
description: Determine whether the array can be split into two subsets with equal sums.
brute: Generate subset sums until finding one equal to half the total.
optimized: If total sum is even, solve 0/1 subset sum for target total/2.

title: Target Sum
description: Assign + or - before every number so the resulting expression equals target. Return the number of ways.
brute: Recursively choose plus or minus for each number.
optimized: Transform to a subset-sum counting problem when mathematically valid, or memoize (index,currentSum).
optimizedCost: Time O(n × sumRange) | Space O(sumRange) or O(n × sumRange)

title: Ones and Zeroes
description: Given binary strings and limits m zeroes and n ones, return the maximum number of strings that can be chosen.
brute: Try every subset and count total zeroes/ones.
optimized: 0/1 knapsack with two capacities. For each string, update dp[zero][one] backward.
optimizedCost: Time O(S × m × n) | Space O(m × n)

title: Coin Change
description: Return the minimum number of coins needed to make an amount, with unlimited copies of each coin.
brute: Recursively try every coin at every remaining amount.
optimized: dp[a] stores the minimum coins for amount a; for each amount/coin update from smaller amounts.

title: Coin Change II
description: Return the number of combinations that make an amount using unlimited coins.
brute: Recursively choose how many copies of each coin to use.
optimized: dp[0]=1; process coins outermost and amounts increasing so each combination is counted once.

title: Combination Sum IV
description: Count ordered combinations of numbers that sum to target; numbers may be reused.
example: Input: nums=[1,2,3], target=4 Input: nums=[1,2,3], target=4 Output: 7
brute: Recursively try every number at every remaining target.
optimized: dp[t] = Σ dp[t-num]; iterate targets outermost because different orders count as different sequences.

title: Rod Cutting
description: Cut a rod into pieces to maximize total selling price, with unlimited use of each piece length.
brute: Recursively try every possible first cut.
optimized: Unbounded-knapsack DP where capacity is rod length and each piece length can be reused.

title: Unique Paths
description: A robot moves only right or down from top-left to bottom-right. Return the number of paths.
brute: Recursively choose right or down at every cell.
optimized: dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1]; compress to one row.

title: Unique Paths II
description: Count right/down paths through a grid containing blocked cells.
brute: Recursively explore right/down paths while stopping at obstacles.
optimized: Same grid DP as Unique Paths, but blocked cells contribute 0 paths.

title: Minimum Path Sum
description: Move right/down from top-left to bottom-right while minimizing the sum of visited grid values.
brute: Recursively explore every right/down path and return the minimum sum.
optimized: dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(top,left).
optimizedCost: Time O(mn) | Space O(n) or in-place O(1) extra

title: Triangle
description: Starting at the triangle top, move to adjacent numbers in the next row. Return the minimum path total.
brute: Recursively choose left-down or right-down at every row.
optimized: Work bottom-up: each cell becomes its value plus the minimum of its two children.
optimizedCost: Time O(number of cells) | Space O(rows) or in-place

title: Maximal Square
description: Find the area of the largest square containing only 1s in a binary matrix.
example: Input: binary matrix Output: largest square area
brute: Treat every 1 as a top-left corner and try larger squares while validating every cell.
optimized: For a 1 cell, square side ending there is 1 + min(top,left,topLeft).
bruteCost: Time high, up to O(mn × min(m,n)^3) naively | Space O(1)

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence; elements need not be contiguous.
brute: At every index choose take or skip while maintaining increasing order.
optimized: Maintain tails[len] as the smallest possible ending value of an increasing subsequence of each length; binary-search where each number belongs.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Russian Doll Envelopes
description: Nest the maximum number of envelopes where both width and height must strictly increase.
brute: Treat each envelope as a state and try all nesting sequences.
optimized: Sort width ascending and equal widths by height descending, then run LIS on heights.
bruteCost: Time exponential or O(n²) DP | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Return the length of the longest sequence appearing in both strings while preserving order, not necessarily contiguously.
brute: Generate subsequences of one string and test whether they are subsequences of the other.
optimized: 2D DP: if characters match, 1 + diagonal; otherwise take max of skipping one character from either string.

title: Longest Common Substring
description: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring common to two strings.
brute: Compare substrings starting from every pair of positions.
optimized: DP where matching characters extend dp[i-1][j-1]; mismatches reset the length to 0.

title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
description: Return the length of the longest palindrome obtainable as a subsequence.
brute: Generate every subsequence and test whether it is a palindrome.
optimized: Use interval DP: matching ends contribute 2 + dp[l+1][r-1]; otherwise skip one end. Equivalent to LCS with the reversed string.
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n²) or O(n) optimized

title: Minimum Insertion Steps to Make String Palindrome
description: Return the minimum insertions needed to make a string a palindrome.
brute: Recursively insert matching characters on either side whenever endpoints differ.
optimized: Minimum insertions equals n - longestPalindromicSubsequenceLength.
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n) to O(n²)

title: Word Break
description: Determine whether a string can be split into dictionary words.
brute: Try every possible next substring recursively.
optimized: dp[i] means prefix s[0..i) can be segmented. For each endpoint, test valid previous split positions/dictionary words.
optimizedCost: Time typically O(n²) plus substring/hash cost | Space O(n)

title: Edit Distance
description: Return the minimum insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to transform one word into another.
brute: On mismatch recursively try insert, delete, and replace.
optimized: 2D DP on prefixes. Matching characters copy diagonal; otherwise 1 + min(insert,delete,replace).

title: Interleaving String
description: Determine whether s3 can be formed by interleaving s1 and s2 while preserving internal order of each.
example: Input: s1="aabcc", s2="dbbca", s3="aadbbcbcac" Output: true
brute: At each position recursively take the next matching character from s1 or s2.
optimized: DP state (i,j) represents whether prefixes s1[0..i) and s2[0..j) can form s3[0..i+j). Optimized: DP state (i,j) represents whether prefixes s1[0..i) and s2[0..j) can form s3[0..i+j).

title: Regular Expression Matching
description: Match a string against a pattern containing . for any character and * for zero or more of the preceding element.
brute: Recursively try consuming characters or skipping/repeating * pattern pieces.
optimized: Memoization/2D DP on (stringIndex, patternIndex); * creates two cases: skip the pair or consume a matching character and stay on pattern.

title: Wildcard Matching
description: Match a string against a pattern where ? matches one character and * matches any sequence, including empty.
brute: Recursively let each * consume zero, one, or many characters.
optimized: DP on prefixes, or greedy two-pointer matching that remembers the most recent * and backtracks its consumed length when needed.
optimizedCost: Time O(mn) DP or often O(m+n) greedy | Space O(n) DP or O(1) greedy

title: Word Break II
description: Return all sentences formed by splitting a string into dictionary words.
example: Input: s="catsanddog", dict=["cat","cats","and","sand","dog"] Output: ["cats and dog","cat sand dog"]
brute: Explore every cut recursively even for suffixes already proven impossible.
optimized: Memoize each start index/suffix to reuse all valid sentence completions from that point.
bruteCost: Time exponential | Space O(n) recursion plus output
optimizedCost: Time exponential output-bound, but repeated subproblems removed | Space output + memoization

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
description: Maximize profit with at most two buy/sell transactions.
brute: Try all possible pairs of non-overlapping transactions.
optimized: Track four states: first buy, first sell, second buy, second sell; update best value of each state per price.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
description: Maximize profit with at most k transactions.
brute: Recursively choose buy/sell days and remaining transactions.
optimized: DP by day, holding state, and transaction count; can be compressed to O(k) state arrays.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock With Cooldown
description: Unlimited transactions are allowed, but after selling you must wait one day before buying again.
brute: Recursively choose buy/sell/skip while tracking cooldown state.
optimized: Track DP states such as hold, sold, and rest, updating them for each day.

title: Burst Balloons
description: Bursting balloon i earns left * nums[i] * right, where left/right are currently adjacent balloons. Maximize total coins.
brute: Try every possible next balloon to burst recursively.
optimized: Think backwards: choose which balloon is burst last inside every interval. Interval DP combines optimal left and right subint ervals.

title: Palindrome Partitioning II
description: Return the minimum cuts needed to partition a string into palindromic substrings.
brute: Generate every palindrome partition and take the minimum number of cuts.
optimized: Precompute palindrome ranges, then DP the minimum cuts for each prefix/end position.
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n²) or improved variants

title: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
description: Cutting a stick costs its current length. Given required cut positions, choose cut order minimizing total cost.
brute: Try every possible next cut recursively.
optimized: Sort cuts and use interval DP: choose the first cut within an interval, pay interval length, plus optimal costs of left/right pieces.
optimizedCost: Time O(c³) where c is number of cuts | Space O(c²)

title: Spiral Matrix
description: Return all matrix elements in clockwise spiral order.
brute: Simulate movement with a visited matrix and direction changes whenever blocked.
optimized: Maintain top, bottom, left, and right boundaries and consume one outer layer at a time.
optimizedCost: Time O(mn) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Spiral Matrix II
description: Generate an n×n matrix filled with 1..n² in clockwise spiral order.
brute: Simulate a moving pointer with a visited matrix.
optimized: Use shrinking four-side boundaries and fill values directly.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n²) visited plus output
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding output

title: Rotate Image
description: Rotate an n×n matrix 90 degrees clockwise in place.
brute: Create a second matrix and set result[col][n-1-row] = matrix[row][col].
optimized: Transpose the matrix across its main diagonal, then reverse every row.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
description: If any cell is zero, set its entire row and column to zero, in place.
brute: Store all zero-row indexes and zero-column indexes in sets, then perform a second pass.
optimized: Use the first row and first column as marker arrays, with separate flags for whether they themselves originally contained zero.

title: Game of Life
description: Update every board cell simultaneously according to Conway's Game of Life neighbor rules.
example: Input: binary board Output: board after one simultaneous generation
brute: Compute the next state in a separate board so updates do not affect neighbor counts.
optimized: Encode transitions in place using temporary states such as 1->0 and 0->1; when counting neighbors, treat transition codes according to their original state. Normalize in a second pass.

title: Valid Sudoku
description: Check whether a partially filled 9×9 Sudoku obeys row, column, and 3×3-box uniqueness rules.
example: Input: partially filled board Output: true or false
brute: For every filled cell, rescan its row, column, and box for duplicates.
optimized: Maintain sets/bitmasks for every row, column, and box while scanning once; reject when a value already exists in any correspo nding structure.
bruteCost: Time O(81 × 27) effectively constant, generalized O(n³) | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n²) or bitmask O(n)

title: Merge Sort
description: Sort an array using divide-and-conquer.
brute: Simpler comparison sorting such as repeated selection/insertion can take quadratic time.
optimized: Split array into halves, recursively sort both halves, then merge the two sorted halves.
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Quick Sort
description: Sort an array by repeatedly partitioning around a pivot.
brute: Use a quadratic simple sort.
optimized: Partition values around a pivot, then recursively sort the left and right partitions.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space depends on algorithm
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) average, O(n²) worst | Space O(log n) average recursion

title: Construct Quad Tree
description: Convert a binary grid into a quad tree. Uniform regions become leaves; mixed regions split into four quadrants.
example: Input: binary square grid Output: corresponding quad-tree root
brute: For every recursive region, scan all cells to check whether they are uniform.
optimized: Precompute 2D prefix sums so any region's number of 1s can be checked in O(1), then recursively split only mixed regions.
bruteCost: Time O(n² log n) in common analysis | Space recursion/tree output
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) preprocessing plus tree construction | Space O(n²) prefix sums/output

title: Kth Largest Element — QuickSelect Alternative
description: Return the kth largest value without fully sorting the array.
brute: Sort the entire array and select the target index.
optimized: Partition as in QuickSort and continue only into the side containing the target index.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space depends on sort
optimizedCost: Time O(n) average, O(n²) worst | Space O(1) iterative

title: Car Pooling
description: Trips add passengers over intervals. Determine whether vehicle capacity is ever exceeded.
brute: For every location/time point, scan all trips to calculate current passengers.
optimized: Add passengers at trip start and subtract them at trip end in a difference array/map, then prefix-sum through events and check capacity.
optimizedCost: Time O(n + range) with array or O(n log n) with ordered events | Space O(range) or O(n)

title: Corporate Flight Bookings
description: Each booking adds a number of seats to every flight in an inclusive range. Return total booked seats for each flight.
brute: For every booking, add seats to every flight in its range.
optimized: Apply diff[start] += seats, diff[end+1] -= seats; one prefix-sum pass produces final totals.

title: Range Addition
description: Apply many range increment operations to an initially zero array and return the final array.
brute: For every update, modify every array element inside its range.
optimized: Use a difference array with one increment at range start and one decrement after range end, then prefix-sum once.

title: LRU Cache
description: Support get and put in O(1) while evicting the least recently used entry when capacity is full.
example: capacity=2 put(1,1), put(2,2), get(1)->1, put(3,3) get(2)->-1
brute: Store entries in a list ordered by recency; every get/put searches the list and moves the entry.
optimized: HashMap gives key-to-node O(1) lookup; doubly linked list maintains most/least recent order with O(1) remove/insert.
bruteCost: Time O(n) per operation | Space O(capacity)
optimizedCost: Time O(1) average per operation | Space O(capacity)

title: LFU Cache
description: Support get/put while evicting the least frequently used key; ties are broken by least recent use.
example: capacity=2 put(1,1), put(2,2), get(1), put(3,3) key 2 is evicted
brute: Store frequency/timestamp metadata and scan all entries to find the eviction candidate.
optimized: Map keys to nodes and map each frequency to a doubly linked list ordered by recency; track the current minimum frequency.
optimizedCost: Time O(1) average get/put | Space O(capacity)

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
description: Support insert, remove, and returning a uniformly random stored value, all in average O(1).
brute: A list gives random access but removal is O(n); a set gives insertion/removal but not indexed random selection.
optimized: Store values in an array/list and value -> index in a hash map. To remove, swap target with the final element, update its index, then pop the end.
bruteCost: Time at least one operation O(n) | Space O(n)

title: Maximum Frequency Stack
description: Push values and pop the value with highest frequency; break ties by most recent push.
brute: On every pop, scan stored values/frequencies and recency to choose the winner.
optimized: Track each value's frequency and maintain a stack for every frequency. maxFreq tells which frequency-stack to pop from.
bruteCost: Time O(n) per pop | Space O(n)

title: Design HashMap
description: Implement a key-value hash map without using built-in hash-table libraries.
brute: Store key-value pairs in a list and linearly search by key.
optimized: Hash keys into buckets and handle collisions with chaining or open addressing; resize if needed.
bruteCost: Time O(n) per operation | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(1) average, O(n) worst | Space O(n)

title: Design Browser History
description: Support visiting a URL, moving back up to steps, and moving forward up to steps.
brute: Use linked structures and manually rebuild forward history after visits.
optimized: Store history in a dynamic array with current index and last valid index. New visit overwrites/discards forward history logically.
bruteCost: Time potentially O(n) operations | Space O(n)

title: Design Twitter
description: Support posting tweets, following/unfollowing users, and returning the 10 most recent tweets from a user's follow network.
brute: Collect all tweets from the user and every followee, then sort the entire collection by timestamp for each feed request.
optimized: Store each user's tweets in reverse chronological order and use a max-heap to k-way merge only the most recent candidates from followed users until 10 tweets are collected.
bruteCost: Time O(T log T) per feed | Space O(T)
optimizedCost: Time roughly O((F+10) log F) per feed | Space O(F) heap plus stored tweets

title: All O(1) Data Structure
description: Support increment/decrement of string keys and retrieving any key with maximum/minimum count, all in O(1) average time.
brute: Maintain key counts in a map and scan all keys whenever min/max is requested.
optimized: Maintain a doubly linked list of count buckets; each bucket holds keys with the same count, while a hash map points every key to its current bucket.
optimizedCost: Time O(1) average for all operations | Space O(n)

title: Tweet Counts Per Frequency
description: Record tweet times and return tweet counts grouped into minute/hour/day buckets over a requested time range.
brute: Store unsorted times and scan every recorded time for every query bucket.
optimized: Store times per tweet name in a sorted structure/list, binary-search the query range, then count relevant times into computed bucket indexes.
bruteCost: Time O(numberTweets + buckets) per query | Space O(numberTweets)
optimizedCost: Time O(log n + matches) per query after ordered storage | Space O(numberTweets)

title: Design Parking System
description: A parking system has fixed numbers of big, medium, and small spots. addCar(type) returns whether a spot is available and consumes it.
brute: Model every individual parking spot as an object/list and scan for a free matching spot.
optimized: Store just three remaining counters and decrement the requested type when positive.
bruteCost: Time O(number of spots) | Space O(number of spots)

title: Range Sum Query Mutable
description: Support changing individual array values and repeatedly querying sums over index ranges.
brute: Keep the array directly. Point update is O(1), but each range query scans the range.
optimized: Segment tree stores sums for intervals; update changes one root-to-leaf path and query combines only relevant segments.
bruteCost: Time O(1) update, O(n) query | Space O(n) array
optimizedCost: Time O(log n) update, O(log n) range query | Space O(n)

title: Range Sum Query 2D Mutable
description: Support point updates in a matrix and repeated rectangular sum queries.
example: Matrix: mutable 2D values update(row,col,val) sumRegion(r1,c1,r2,c2) -> rectangle sum
brute: Update cell directly and sum every cell in each requested rectangle.
optimized: Use a 2D Fenwick Tree or 2D Segment Tree so updates and prefix-sum queries are logarithmic in both dimensions.
bruteCost: Time O(1) update, O(rows × cols) query | Space O(1) extra
optimizedCost: Time O(log R × log C) update/query | Space O(RC)

title: Range Sum Query 2D Immutable
description: Preprocess an immutable matrix to answer rectangular sum queries quickly.
example: Query rectangle: (2,1) to (4,3) Output: sum of that rectangle
brute: Sum every cell inside the rectangle for each query.
optimized: Build a 2D prefix sum. Rectangle sum uses four prefix values by inclusion-exclusion.
bruteCost: Time O(rows × cols) per query | Space O(1)
optimizedCost: Time O(RC) preprocessing, O(1) query | Space O(RC)

title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
description: For every array position, return how many later values are smaller than it.
brute: For every index, scan all values to its right and count smaller ones.
optimized: Coordinate-compress values, scan from right to left, query a Fenwick Tree for how many smaller ranks have been inserted, then add the cu rrent rank.
bruteCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(1) excluding output
optimizedCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)

title: Odd or Even Using Bits
description: Determine whether an integer is odd or even using bit operations.
brute: Use modulo: n % 2.
optimized: Check the least significant bit using (n & 1). 1 means odd; 0 means even.

title: Sparse Number
description: Determine whether a number's binary representation contains no adjacent set bits.
example: Input: 5 (101) Output: true Input: 6 (110) Output: false
