brute: Convert to binary string and search for "11".
optimized: Adjacent set bits exist when n & (n >> 1) is non-zero.
bruteCost: Time O(log n) | Space O(log n)
optimizedCost: Time O(1) for fixed-width integer | Space O(1)

title: Majority Element II
description: Return all values appearing more than n/3 times. There can be at most two such values.
brute: Count all values with a hash map and return counts greater than n/3.
optimized: Extended Boyer-Moore voting keeps at most two candidates, followed by one verification pass.

title: Distribute Candies
description: A person receives half of the candies and wants the maximum number of distinct candy types possible.
brute: Try all subsets of size n/2 and count distinct types.
optimized: Count total distinct types. Answer is min(distinctTypes, n/2).

title: Logger Rate Limiter
description: A message should be printed only if the same message was not printed during the previous 10 seconds.
example: shouldPrint(1,"foo") -> true shouldPrint(2,"foo") -> false shouldPrint(11,"foo") -> true
brute: Store all past log events and scan backward for the latest equal message.
optimized: HashMap message -> nextAllowedTimestamp or last-printed timestamp.
bruteCost: Time O(n) per request | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(1) average per request | Space O(number of active messages)

title: Valid Palindrome II
description: Determine whether a string can become a palindrome after deleting at most one character.
brute: Delete each possible character and test the resulting string for palindrome.
optimized: Use opposite pointers. At the first mismatch, check either skipping the left character or skipping the right character.

title: Find the Celebrity
description: In a group, a celebrity is known by everyone but knows nobody. Find the celebrity if one exists.
example: Input: knows(a,b) relation for n people Output: celebrity index or -1
brute: For every person, check whether they know nobody and everyone else knows them.
optimized: Eliminate candidates in one pass: if candidate knows i, candidate cannot be celebrity, so set candidate=i. Then verify the final candidate.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) relation checks after elimination/verification | Space O(1)

title: Trapping Rain Water II
description: Given a 2D elevation map, return how much water can be trapped after raining.
brute: For each cell, try to determine the minimum surrounding boundary through repeated searches in all directions; local left/righ t logic is insufficient in 2D.
optimized: Put all boundary cells into a min-heap. Expand inward from the lowest boundary; a lower neighbor traps boundaryHeight - neighborHeight, then enters the heap with the effective higher boundary.
optimizedCost: Time O(rows × cols × log(rows×cols)) | Space O(rows × cols)

title: Longest Substring With At Most K Distinct Characters
description: Return the longest substring containing at most k distinct characters.
brute: Start at every index and extend while counting distinct characters.
optimized: Variable sliding window with a frequency map; shrink while distinct count exceeds k.

title: Longest Substring With At Least K Repeating Characters
description: Find the longest substring in which every character appears at least k times.
brute: Check every substring and verify all character frequencies.
optimized: One approach is divide-and-conquer: any character occurring fewer than k times cannot belong to a valid answer, so split around such characters. A sliding -window-by-distinct-count solution is also possible.
optimizedCost: Time typically O(n × alphabet) for the sliding-window approach | Space O(alphabet)

title: Contains Duplicate II
description: Determine whether equal values occur at indexes whose distance is at most k.
brute: For every index, compare up to the next k positions.
optimized: Maintain a sliding HashSet containing only the last k values.

title: Contains Duplicate III
description: Determine whether two indexes are within indexDiff and their values differ by at most valueDiff.
example: Input: nums=[1,2,3,1], indexDiff=3, valueDiff=0 Output: true
brute: Compare every pair whose index distance is within the limit.
optimized: Maintain an ordered set for the last indexDiff values and query the nearest value using floor/ceiling; bucketization can also achieve average O(n).
optimizedCost: Time O(n log indexDiff) with TreeSet | Space O(indexDiff)

title: Diet Plan Performance
description: For each fixed-size k-day calorie window, gain a point if its sum is above an upper threshold and lose a point if below a lower threshold.
example: Input: calories=[1,2,3,4,5], k=1, lower=3, upper=3 Output: 0
brute: Recalculate every k-day sum from scratch.
optimized: Fixed sliding window: add the incoming day's calories and remove the outgoing day's calories.

title: Minimum Window Subsequence
description: Find the shortest substring of S that contains T as a subsequence.
brute: Check every substring of S and test whether T is its subsequence.
optimized: Scan forward to find an end position containing the full subsequence, then scan backward to shrink to the smallest start; repeat from the next possible position. DP is another standard solution.
optimizedCost: Time around O(nm) worst case | Space O(1) for two-scan version

title: Count Unique Characters of All Substrings of a Given String
description: For every substring, count characters that occur exactly once in that substring; return the total across all substrings.
brute: Generate every substring and count its character frequencies.
optimized: Compute each character occurrence's contribution. If the previous same position is p and next is q, that occurrence is unique in (i-p) × (q-i) substrings.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(alphabet) or occurrence lists

title: Longest Subsequence Repeated K Times
description: Find the longest string that appears as a subsequence of s at least k times when repeated k times.
brute: Generate subsequences and test whether each candidate repeated k times is a subsequence of s.
optimized: Candidate characters must have frequency at least k. Build candidate strings level by level with BFS/backtracking and keep only candidates whose candidate × k is a subsequence of s.
optimizedCost: Time exponential in the small candidate length, heavily pruned by frequency | Space candidate queue/search state

title: Longest Nice Substring
description: A substring is nice if for every letter present, both lowercase and uppercase forms are present. Return the longest nice subs tring.
brute: Check every substring and compare lowercase/uppercase presence.
optimized: If a character lacks its opposite case in the current substring, no valid answer can cross that character. Split there recursively and return the longer side.
optimizedCost: Time about O(n²) worst case | Space O(n) recursion

title: Sort a Stack
description: Sort a stack using only stack operations, often with recursion or one auxiliary stack.
brute: Pop all elements into an array, sort the array, and push them back.
optimized: Use an auxiliary stack like insertion sort, moving elements back until the current value can be inserted in sorted position.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space O(n)
optimizedCost: Time O(n²) | Space O(n) auxiliary stack

title: First Non-Repeating Character in a Stream
description: After every incoming character, report the first character seen exactly once so far.
example: Input stream: a, a, b, c Output sequence: a, #, b, b
brute: After each new character, rescan the complete stream and frequencies to find the first unique value.
optimized: Maintain character frequencies and a queue of candidate unique characters. Remove queue front while its frequency is greater than one.

title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String
description: Repeatedly remove adjacent equal character pairs until no more pairs remain.
brute: Repeatedly scan and delete adjacent duplicates until stable.
optimized: Use a stack/string builder. If current character equals the top, pop it; otherwise push it.

title: Linked List in Binary Tree
description: Determine whether the linked-list values appear as a downward path in a binary tree.
example: Input: head=4->2->8, binary tree containing a downward 4,2,8 path Output: true
brute: From every tree node, recursively try matching the complete linked list downward.
optimized: DFS every tree node as a potential start with early mismatch pruning; advanced versions combine the linked -list pattern with KMP prefix information to avoid repeated matching.
bruteCost: Time O(treeNodes × listLength) worst case | Space O(treeHeight)
optimizedCost: Time typical DFS O(NL), KMP-enhanced near O(N+L) | Space O(H+L)

title: Special Keyboard / Four Keys Keyboard
description: With keys for A, Select All, Copy, and Paste, find the maximum number of As producible using N key presses.
brute: Recursively try every possible key operation sequence while tracking clipboard and screen state.
optimized: DP over total key presses. For each possible point to start Select All + Copy + repeated Paste, compute the best multiplication of an earlier result.

title: Basic Calculator II
description: Evaluate an expression containing non-negative integers, +, -, *, /, and spaces without parentheses.
brute: Repeatedly locate and evaluate multiplication/division first, rewrite the string, then process addition/subtraction.
optimized: Scan once while keeping the previous operator. Immediately resolve * and /; defer + and - using a stack or running lastTerm.
optimizedCost: Time O(n) | Space O(n) with stack or O(1) using last-term technique

title: Basic Calculator III
description: Evaluate an arithmetic expression containing +, -, *, /, parentheses, and spaces.
brute: Repeatedly find innermost parentheses and rewrite/evaluate substrings.
optimized: Recursive-descent parsing or stack-based parsing handles parentheses and operator precedence in one pass.

title: Wiggle Sort
description: Rearrange an array so nums[0] <= nums[1] >= nums[2] <= nums[3]....
example: Input: [3,5,2,1,6,4] Output: one valid wiggle order such as [3,5,1,6,2,4]
brute: Sort the array and swap adjacent pairs.
optimized: Scan once. At even/odd positions, swap adjacent values whenever the required <= or >= relation is violated.
bruteCost: Time O(n log n) | Space depends on sort
